title: SEDarc ESRC PhD Studentships 2027 in the UK | Fully Funded Doctoral Opportunities
summary: The South East Doctoral Training Arc (SEDarc) is offering Economic and Social Research Council (ESRC)-funded PhD studentships for September 2027 entry , providing opportunities for talented researchers in the social sciences to undertake doctoral study at one of six participating universities in London and South East England. The studentships are open to UK and international students and include UK tuition fees and a stipend at the UKRI rate. For successful overseas applicants, the SEDarc institutions will cover the difference between UK home and international tuition fees, except for the University of Reading . The SEDarc deadline is 29 January 2027 at 16:00 GMT , although applicants must first complete the institutional application process, and each participating university has its own deadline and procedure. Participating Universities Students can be based at one of six higher education institutions: University of Kent Kingston University University of Reading Royal Holloway, University of London University of Surrey University of Sussex SEDarc also works with non-higher-education partner organisations to strengthen the research and training opportunities available to doctoral students. SEDarc Research Pathways SEDarc s doctoral training model combines advanced research skills training, placements and an individual research project within one of five interdisciplinary, challenge-led pathways: Living Sustainably Healthy Thriving Communities Inclusive Economic Growth Secure, Effective, Trusted Institutions Transformative Technologies for Society These pathways provide a framework for research addressing major social, economic, environmental, institutional and technological challenges. Funding and Benefits The standard SEDarc PhD lasts 3.5 years full-time , including a three-month placement , or the part-time equivalent. The funding package covers: UK tuition fees A UKRI-rate stipend Three-month placement Research and skills training Individual doctoral research For eligible students without a relevant social-science Master s degree, potential funding for an approved Master s course within the SEDarc consortium The UKRI has not yet announced the 2027/28 tuition fee and stipend rates. For reference, the 2026/27 rates were: UK tuition fees: £5,238 UKRI stipend: £21,805 London-weighted stipend: £23,805 where applicable The 2027/28 figures may therefore differ. Funding for International Students SEDarc accepts international applications. For successful overseas applicants, the SEDarc institutions will cover the difference between UK home tuition fees and international tuition fees. However, an important exception applies: the University of Reading does not cover this difference . International applicants should therefore carefully check the financial arrangements of their chosen institution before applying. Ring-Fenced Scholarships SEDarc is committed to equality, diversity and inclusion throughout the doctoral journey. The programme states that it will reserve up to three ring-fenced scholarships for eligible home students from certain Black, Asian and Minority Ethnic groups . Applicants interested in these ring-fenced studentships should review the specific eligibility criteria published by SEDarc. Who Can Apply? The SEDarc PhD studentships are open to: UK students International students Applicants working across the social sciences Prospective PhD researchers who meet the academic requirements of their chosen institution and programme Applicants who do not already hold a Master s degree in the social sciences may also be eligible for funding to undertake an approved Master s course within the SEDarc consortium. Eligibility for this additional Master s funding depends on the relevant requirements. How to Apply Applicants cannot apply directly to SEDarc without institutional nomination. Students must first be nominated by one of the six SEDarc universities . The application process therefore involves: Choose one of the six participating SEDarc institutions. Identify a suitable doctoral research area and SEDarc pathway. Contact the SEDarc administrator at your chosen university. Follow that institution s application process and deadline. Complete the institutional stage of the application. Obtain nomination from the university. Submit the SEDarc studentship application by the SEDarc deadline. Because the six universities have different institutional deadlines and procedures, applicants should contact their chosen university as early as possible. University Contacts Kingston University: hssce-research@kingston.ac.uk Royal Holloway, University of London: esrcdtp@rhul.ac.uk University of Kent: kentgrc@kent.ac.uk University of Reading: doctoralstudentshipsofficer@reading.ac.uk University of Surrey: doctoralcollege@surrey.ac.uk University of Sussex: pgr-scholarships@sussex.ac.uk Application Deadline The SEDarc studentship application deadline is: 29 January 2027 at 16:00 GMT Applicants should note that this is the SEDarc deadline. The university they choose will have its own earlier institutional deadline and application process. Applicants should therefore not wait until January 2027 before contacting their chosen institution. Important Funding Notice SEDarc s ESRC Doctoral Training Partnership is subject to a mid-term review in 2026 . According to the programme information, the number of studentships may be revised depending on the findings of the review. Allocations for the 2027 cohort are expected to be confirmed around January 2027 . Conclusion The SEDarc ESRC PhD studentships provide funded doctoral study opportunities for UK and international researchers in the social sciences, with placements, research training and interdisciplinary research pathways forming part of the programme. Students can apply through one of six participating universities: Kent, Kingston, Reading, Royal Holloway, Surrey or Sussex. The standard PhD is 3.5 years full-time and includes a three-month placement. Funding covers UK tuition fees and provides a UKRI-rate stipend, while arrangements for international tuition fees vary by institution. The main SEDarc application deadline is 29 January 2027 at 16:00 GMT , but applicants must first meet the separate institutional deadline and nomination requirements of their selected university. title: PPG Research Fellowship 2026 in the USA | $50 Per Hour for Early-Career Researchers
summary: Partners for Public Good (PPG) is accepting applications for its 2026 Research Fellowship, a six-month, project-based opportunity for early-career researchers interested in improving government effectiveness through rigorous, policy-relevant research. The fellowship is designed for researchers who want to contribute directly to research on public procurement, local government operations, technology, regulatory systems, infrastructure and government capacity. Selected fellows will work remotely from within the United States for approximately 15 to 25 hours per week and will receive compensation of $50 per hour , with benefits as required by applicable state or local law. The fellowship is expected to begin in October 2026 , and applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis. The final application deadline is September 28, 2026 , at close of business. About the PPG Research Fellowship The PPG Research Fellowship is a six-month programme that provides early-career researchers with dedicated time, mentorship and practical experience conducting research connected to government effectiveness. Fellows will work on one of five predetermined high-priority research topics related to public procurement and local government operations. Throughout the fellowship, participants will conduct policy-relevant background research, apply rigorous research methods to collect and analyse data, and collaborate with PPG staff and other fellows. The programme is designed not only to generate useful research for governments but also to help fellows develop their own research portfolios through publications, policy briefs, datasets and other professional outputs. About Partners for Public Good Partners for Public Good (PPG) is a nonpartisan organisation that works alongside state and local governments to strengthen the operational systems that determine whether policies translate into results for residents. Its work covers areas including: Procurement Staffing Budgeting Technology Government operations Applied research Implementation Rather than simply providing recommendations, PPG works directly with government staff during implementation and remains engaged until meaningful changes have been achieved. Through its implementation work, applied research and Procurement Excellence Network, PPG shares knowledge and tools that can be applied across different jurisdictions. The organisation s Procurement Excellence Network includes more than 3,000 government professionals. Why the Fellowship Focuses on Local Government Local governments play a critical role in translating public policy into services and outcomes that residents experience every day. Areas such as transportation, infrastructure, emergency services and school food depend on effective local government systems and operations. However, there remains a need for more rigorous research examining how local governments manage procurement, budgeting, technology and staffing capacity, as well as how these operations are influenced by state and federal policies and regulations. The PPG Research Fellowship aims to support a new generation of researchers who are interested in using evidence and research to improve government effectiveness. The programme provides fellows with an opportunity to investigate practical government challenges while producing research that can contribute to broader discussions about public-sector reform. Fellowship Structure The fellowship lasts for six months. Fellows will work on a defined research project under the guidance of PPG staff and alongside two other fellows. The programme combines independent research with collaboration and professional development. Participants will take part in activities such as: Coaching calls Research team meetings Collaborative research activities Professional development opportunities Research discussions with PPG staff Fellows will also receive support in translating their research into public-facing outputs, including draft publications and policy briefs. Before the fellowship begins, PPG and each selected fellow will agree on: Work hours Project goals Expected deliverables Data access Data use Data rights Data ownership The work schedule is flexible within the agreed 15–25-hour-per-week commitment. Five Research Topics Applicants can express interest in one or two of the five research projects available through the fellowship. 1. Understanding Public Procurement Through Municipal Data Public procurement is an important mechanism through which governments use public resources to provide services, infrastructure and other outcomes for residents. However, procurement practices, systems and publicly available information can differ significantly from one jurisdiction to another. This research project will examine publicly available information about local government procurement to develop a better understanding of procurement practices across U.S. cities. The fellow will contribute to research designed to strengthen understanding of how governments purchase goods and services while identifying opportunities for further research and analysis. 2. The Compliance Web: Layered Governance and Local Implementation Local governments operate within a complex system of federal, state and local laws, regulations, funding requirements and administrative procedures. While these requirements can establish important protections and standards, they can also create administrative burdens, uncertainty and challenges for effective implementation. This project will focus on one area, such as permitting, transit infrastructure or school food procurement, to examine how the complex compliance web affects local government operations and project delivery. The research will explore where federal and state policies support or constrain local implementation and how policy design could better support effective government delivery. 3. Emerging Technology and Government Operations State and local governments are increasingly exploring artificial intelligence and other emerging technologies to support internal operations and their workforce. These technologies may also provide new ways to understand how public servants interact with government systems and processes. This research project will explore what the use of AI and emerging technologies can reveal about government operations, organisational capacity and opportunities for improvement. The fellow will contribute to developing and testing new approaches to studying how government work is performed. 4. Innovative Approaches to Public Purchasing Governments have multiple tools and approaches available for purchasing goods and services. Different purchasing approaches can involve different advantages, limitations and trade-offs. This project will examine emerging procurement trends, with particular attention to cooperative purchasing. The research will explore how and why different approaches are being used across jurisdictions and consider their implications for: Government efficiency Market participation Public procurement systems The broader procurement ecosystem 5. Building Local Capacity for Stormwater Management Communities across the United States are exploring different ways to improve their ability to manage stormwater and respond to infrastructure and resilience needs. Approaches vary depending on local circumstances, governance structures and state and federal policy environments. This research project will examine how communities develop and finance stormwater management capacity. Fellows will identify patterns across jurisdictions and generate insights that can inform future research and practical approaches to stormwater management. Fellowship Deliverables Each fellow will be expected to complete approximately two to three deliverables during the fellowship. Depending on the research project, deliverables may include: A topic-specific literature review A dataset compiled from publicly available information and supporting documentation A dataset developed through primary data collection Survey or interview instruments A draft research publication A policy brief A conference submission These outputs can provide fellows with practical research experience while strengthening their professional and academic portfolios. Fellowship Location and Working Hours The fellowship is a remote opportunity. The position can be undertaken from a flexible location within the United States, but fellows must have access to a major U.S. airport because the programme includes an in-person research retreat. Fellows will work between 15 and 25 hours per week . The exact working hours will be agreed upon between PPG and each selected fellow before the fellowship begins. Fellowship Compensation Selected fellows will be compensated at a rate of: $50 per hour The fellowship requires approximately 15–25 hours of work per week. Benefits will be provided where required by applicable state or local law. The compensation structure provides fellows with paid research experience while allowing them to maintain other academic or professional commitments within the requirements of the programme. Who Can Apply? The fellowship is intended for early-career researchers and professionals with relevant research or policy experience. Potential applicants may include: Graduate students Postdoctoral researchers Early-career faculty Research staff Policy staff Researchers affiliated with universities Researchers affiliated with think tanks Researchers affiliated with nonprofits Professionals with comparable research or policy experience Applicants may maintain an affiliation with a university, think tank, nonprofit or other research or policy organisation during the fellowship, provided they can meet the required time commitments and deliverables. Applicants who do not have an institutional affiliation are also welcome to apply. Application Requirements Applicants must submit the following materials: 1. Resume or CV Applicants must submit a resume or curriculum vitae of no more than two pages . The document should clearly present the applicant s relevant academic, research, professional and policy experience. 2. Letter of Interest Applicants must submit a letter of interest addressing specific questions. The letter should explain: Which one or two research projects the applicant is interested in and why. Why the applicant is qualified to undertake the selected project. How the applicant would approach the proposed research. Applicants interested in two projects may submit a letter of up to three pages and should clearly identify their first-choice project. Applicants interested in only one project should follow the two-page limit. 3. Work Sample Applicants must provide a work sample demonstrating their research skills and expertise. The work sample may be: A published research publication A research publication under review Another relevant research product Applicants should select a work sample that provides strong evidence of their ability to conduct and communicate rigorous research. Application Deadline The final deadline to apply for the PPG Research Fellowship is: September 28, 2026 PPG will review applications on a rolling basis. All applications received by the close of business on September 28, 2026 will be considered. Applicants are encouraged to submit their materials as early as possible because applications are reviewed on a rolling basis. Expected Start Date The desired start date for the fellowship is: October 2026 Selected fellows will work with PPG before the start of the programme to establish expectations regarding working hours, research goals, deliverables and data-related matters. Equal Employment Opportunity Partners for Public Good is an equal opportunity employer. The organisation states that all qualified applicants will receive consideration without regard to race, colour, religion, sex, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status or any other characteristic protected by law. PPG is also committed to including qualified individuals with disabilities in its hiring process. Applicants who require reasonable accommodation to participate in the application or interview process can contact the organisation through the contact information provided in the original application announcement. How to Apply for the PPG Research Fellowship Interested applicants should prepare all required materials before submitting their application . The application process includes: Review the five available research topics. Select the one or two projects that best match your interests and experience. Identify your first-choice project if applying for two. Prepare a resume or CV of no more than two pages. Prepare the required letter of interest. Select an appropriate research work sample. Review all application requirements carefully. Submit the complete application before the September 28, 2026 deadline. Conclusion The PPG Research Fellowship 2026 offers early-career researchers an opportunity to gain practical experience conducting policy-relevant research focused on government effectiveness and local government operations. Over six months, fellows will work alongside PPG staff and other researchers on one of five research topics covering public procurement, regulatory compliance, emerging technology, public purchasing and stormwater management. The programme combines independent research, collaboration, mentorship and professional development, while giving participants opportunities to produce literature reviews, datasets, publications, policy briefs and conference submissions. Selected fellows will work remotely for 15–25 hours per week and receive $50 per hour , with benefits as required by applicable law. The fellowship is expected to begin in October 2026. Researchers interested in contributing to evidence-based improvements in government operations should consider preparing their application early. The final deadline is September 28, 2026 . title: Penn State HDFS PhD Graduate Program 2027 | Application Open for Graduate Study
summary: The Department of Human Development and Family Studies (HDFS) at Pennsylvania State University has opened applications for its Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) graduate programme. The programme provides an opportunity for students interested in advanced graduate study in the behavioral sciences, human development and family studies. Applicants interested in joining the programme must apply through the Penn State Graduate School admissions portal and select the Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) degree. The application deadline is December 1. Prospective applicants are encouraged to carefully review the programme requirements and prepare all required documents before submitting their applications. Applicants outside the United States should also take the application deadline and Penn State s Eastern Standard Time zone into account when submitting their applications. About the Penn State HDFS Graduate Programme The Human Development and Family Studies graduate programme is designed for students pursuing advanced academic and research training in areas related to human development, family studies and the behavioral sciences. The programme follows a doctoral pathway. HDFS does not offer a terminal master s programme. Students who enter the programme with a bachelor s degree are required to complete a master s degree en route to the doctoral degree. Applicants should therefore select the Ph.D. degree when completing the graduate application rather than applying for a standalone master s programme. Application Deadline The application deadline for the Penn State HDFS graduate programme is: December 1 Applicants are responsible for ensuring that their applications are submitted by the deadline. Penn State is located in the Eastern Standard Time zone. Applicants submitting their applications from outside the United States should account for the time difference when determining when to submit their applications. It is recommended that applicants avoid waiting until the final hours of the deadline to submit their materials. How to Apply Applications must be submitted through the Penn State Graduate School admissions portal . University policy allows an applicant to apply to only one graduate degree programme at a time. Applicants interested in HDFS should therefore ensure that they select the Doctor of Philosophy (Ph.D.) degree when completing the application. The application process will guide applicants through the general requirements established by the Graduate School as well as the programme-specific materials required by HDFS. Applicants should review all requirements carefully before submitting their application. Required Application Materials Applicants to the HDFS graduate programme are expected to provide several documents as part of their application. The required programme-specific materials include: 1. Scientific Writing Sample Applicants are required to submit a scientific writing sample as part of the application. The writing sample should demonstrate the applicant s ability to communicate academic or research-related ideas effectively and provide evidence of their writing and analytical abilities. 2. Official Transcripts Applicants must provide official academic transcripts as required by the university. Transcripts allow the admissions committee to assess an applicant s previous academic preparation and educational background. Applicants should ensure that their academic records meet Penn State Graduate School requirements. 3. Curriculum Vitae or Résumé Applicants must submit a curriculum vitae (CV) or résumé outlining their academic, professional, research and other relevant experiences. Applicants should ensure that the document clearly presents experiences that are relevant to their intended graduate study. 4. Statement of Professional and Career Plans Applicants are required to submit a statement describing their professional and career plans. This statement provides an opportunity for applicants to explain their academic and professional objectives and how doctoral study relates to their long-term goals. Applicants should use the statement to clearly communicate their motivation for pursuing graduate education and their intended career direction. 5. Three Letters of Recommendation Applicants must provide three letters of recommendation. Recommendation letters are an important part of the application because they can provide the admissions committee with additional insight into an applicant s academic preparation, capabilities and potential for success in graduate study. Applicants should select recommenders who are familiar with their academic, research or professional abilities. Applicants from Outside the United States International applicants may have additional requirements as part of the Penn State Graduate School admissions process. Applicants from outside the United States should carefully review the university s requirements for international applicants and ensure that all required documentation is provided. International applicants should also pay particular attention to application deadlines and time-zone differences when submitting their applications. GRE Scores Are Not Required The HDFS graduate programme does not require GRE scores as part of the application. The department uses a holistic review process to evaluate each applicant s potential to succeed in the programme. Applicants will receive full consideration regardless of whether they submit GRE scores. Although GRE scores are not required, some applicants may choose to submit them if they believe the scores would provide additional evidence of their potential for graduate study in the behavioral sciences. For example, submitting GRE scores may be useful for applicants whose undergraduate major is not closely related to the HDFS graduate curriculum or applicants returning to graduate school after working in another field. In such circumstances, an applicant s academic transcripts and recommendation letters may not fully demonstrate their preparation for graduate study in the behavioral sciences. Applicants may therefore consider whether additional materials, including GRE scores, would strengthen their application. Holistic Application Review The HDFS programme evaluates applications using a holistic review process. This means applicants are considered based on the overall strength and potential demonstrated through their application rather than solely on one component such as standardized test scores. Applicants should therefore focus on presenting a complete application that accurately communicates their academic preparation, research interests, experiences, professional objectives and potential for success in graduate study. Who Should Apply? The programme may be suitable for students and professionals interested in pursuing advanced academic and research training related to human development, family studies and the behavioral sciences. Applicants should carefully assess their academic background and professional objectives against the HDFS programme before applying. Students entering with a bachelor s degree should be prepared to complete a master s degree en route to the Ph.D. Important Things Applicants Should Know Before submitting an application, prospective students should keep the following points in mind: The application deadline is December 1. Applications must be submitted through the Penn State Graduate School admissions portal. Applicants may apply to only one graduate degree programme at a time under university policy. HDFS applicants should select the Ph.D. degree. HDFS does not offer a terminal master s programme. Students entering with a bachelor s degree are required to complete a master s degree en route to the doctoral degree. A scientific writing sample is required. Official transcripts are required. Applicants must provide a CV or résumé. A statement of professional and career plans is required. Three letters of recommendation are required. GRE scores are not required. International applicants should review the additional requirements applicable to applicants from outside the United States. Applicants submitting from another time zone should account for Penn State s Eastern Standard Time zone. Contact for Application Questions Applicants who have questions about the application process can contact the HDFS academic programme coordinator. Applicants with questions about whether GRE scores would strengthen their application or other questions about improving their application may also contact the HDFS Admissions Committee. Conclusion The Penn State Human Development and Family Studies Ph.D. programme provides an opportunity for applicants seeking advanced graduate education and research training in the behavioral sciences and related areas. The programme follows a doctoral pathway, and students entering with a bachelor s degree are required to complete a master s degree en route to the Ph.D. Applicants must submit their applications through the Penn State Graduate School admissions portal and provide the required academic and supporting materials. The application requires a scientific writing sample, official transcripts, a CV or résumé, a statement of professional and career plans and three letters of recommendation. GRE scores are not required, and applications are evaluated through a holistic review process. Interested applicants should begin preparing their application materials early and ensure that their complete application is submitted by the December 1 deadline , taking Penn State s Eastern Standard Time zone into account. title: UPEACE Somalia 2026 Admissions and Scholarships | Master’s and PhD Programmes
summary: The University for Peace (UPEACE) Somalia has opened admissions for its 2026 academic enrolment, providing an opportunity for students and professionals from Somalia, East Africa and other parts of the world to pursue postgraduate studies in peace, governance, development, sustainability, humanitarian action, law, human rights and related fields. The 2026 admissions include a range of Master’s and Doctoral programmes delivered online, making the programmes accessible to applicants who may be unable to relocate for their studies. In addition to the academic programmes, UPEACE Somalia has announced special scholarship opportunities that can significantly reduce tuition costs for successful applicants. The available scholarships include discounts of up to 30% for Master’s programmes, 50% for PhD programmes and 60% for UPEACE alumni. The scholarship deadline is 15 September 2026. About UPEACE Somalia The University for Peace Somalia was established in 2018 as part of efforts to provide advanced academic programmes that respond to Somalia’s development and peacebuilding needs. The institution is associated with the University for Peace, which was established in 1980 through United Nations General Assembly Resolution 35/55. The University for Peace is headquartered in Costa Rica and focuses on education and research related to peace, conflict resolution, sustainable development and international cooperation. UPEACE Somalia provides programmes designed to equip students with knowledge and skills relevant to some of the major challenges facing Somalia, East Africa and the wider international community. The programmes are offered online and are open to students from Somalia, East Africa and beyond. UPEACE Somalia 2026 Doctoral Programmes Applicants interested in pursuing doctoral-level studies can choose from several programmes covering peace, governance, leadership, sustainable development, maritime security and environmental challenges. The available Doctoral programmes include: 1. Doctoral Programme in Peace, Governance and Development This programme focuses on the relationship between peace, governance and sustainable development. It is particularly relevant to individuals interested in research and professional work addressing conflict, governance systems, development challenges and peacebuilding. 2. Doctoral Programme in Leadership and Sustainable Development This programme explores leadership and its role in promoting sustainable development. It may be relevant to professionals and researchers interested in leadership, development policy and long-term approaches to addressing social and economic challenges. 3. Doctoral Programme in Blue Economy and Maritime Security The programme focuses on issues surrounding the sustainable use of marine resources and maritime security. It may be particularly relevant to applicants interested in the blue economy, maritime governance, environmental sustainability and security. 4. Doctoral Programme in Land Degradation and Desertification This programme addresses environmental challenges associated with land degradation and desertification. It is particularly relevant to research and development priorities in regions affected by drought, environmental degradation and changing climate conditions. UPEACE Somalia 2026 Master’s Programmes Applicants seeking Master’s-level study can choose from several programmes covering peace, development, environment, international law, humanitarian action, energy and water resources. The available Master’s programmes include: 1. Master of Arts in Peace, Governance and Development This programme combines peace studies with governance and development, providing an opportunity for students to develop knowledge relevant to conflict prevention, peacebuilding, governance and development policy. 2. Master of Arts in Environment, Development and Peace This programme brings together environmental issues, development and peace. It is relevant to individuals interested in the links between environmental challenges, sustainable development and peacebuilding. 3. Master of Arts in International Law and Human Rights This programme focuses on international legal frameworks and human rights. It may be suitable for applicants seeking advanced knowledge of international law, human rights protection and related areas of policy and practice. 4. Master of Arts in Disaster Resilience and Humanitarian Action This programme focuses on disaster resilience and humanitarian responses. It is particularly relevant to individuals working or intending to work in humanitarian assistance, disaster management, resilience building and emergency response. 5. Master of Science in Energy, Economics and Governance This programme examines the relationship between energy, economics and governance. It provides an opportunity for students interested in energy policy, economic development, governance and sustainable energy systems. 6. Master of Arts in Sustainable Water Resources Management This programme focuses on the sustainable management of water resources. It is relevant to applicants interested in water governance, environmental sustainability, development and the management of water resources. UPEACE Somalia Scholarship Opportunities 2026 One of the major features of the 2026 admissions announcement is the availability of special scholarship opportunities. According to the announcement, the scholarship opportunities include: 30% scholarships for Master’s programmes. 50% scholarships for PhD programmes. 60% scholarships for UPEACE alumni. These scholarships can help reduce the financial cost of postgraduate education for eligible applicants. Applicants should carefully review the scholarship conditions and admission requirements before submitting their applications. UPEACE Somalia 2026 Admission Requirements Applicants for the Doctoral programmes are required to have a certified Master’s degree and transcripts, in addition to other requirements that may apply during the application process. For the Master’s programmes, applicants are required to have a certified Bachelor’s degree and transcripts, alongside any additional requirements specified by UPEACE Somalia. Applicants should ensure that their academic documents are properly prepared and certified where required before beginning the application process. Additional admission requirements may vary depending on the selected programme. Who Can Apply? The UPEACE Somalia 2026 admissions are open to applicants from Somalia, East Africa and beyond. The programmes are therefore relevant to prospective postgraduate students from different countries who meet the academic requirements for their selected programme. Applicants should confirm the specific requirements for their chosen Master’s or Doctoral programme before applying. Study Format The programmes offered through UPEACE Somalia are delivered online. This provides students with an opportunity to pursue postgraduate education without necessarily relocating to another country for their studies. The online format may be particularly useful for working professionals, researchers and students who need to combine their studies with professional or other responsibilities. Why Consider UPEACE Somalia? UPEACE Somalia’s programmes are focused on areas that are closely connected to major development, peace and sustainability challenges. Depending on the programme selected, students can pursue advanced studies in areas such as: Peacebuilding and conflict transformation Governance and development Sustainable development Environmental management International law Human rights Humanitarian action Disaster resilience Energy governance Water resources management Blue economy Maritime security Land degradation and desertification These fields can be relevant to careers in government, international organisations, development agencies, humanitarian organisations, research institutions, civil society and other sectors. Application Deadline The scholarship deadline for the UPEACE Somalia 2026 admissions is: 15 September 2026 Applicants interested in benefiting from the announced scholarship opportunities should ensure that they submit their applications and complete any required steps before the stated deadline. How to Apply for UPEACE Somalia 2026 Interested applicants should access the UPEACE Somalia admissions platform to review the available programmes, admission requirements and application procedures. Applicants should: Review the available Master’s and Doctoral programmes. Select a programme that matches their academic background and career interests. Check the specific admission requirements for the selected programme. Prepare the required academic documents, including certified degrees and transcripts where applicable. Review the available scholarship opportunities and their conditions. Submit the application through the official admissions platform. Complete any additional steps requested by UPEACE Somalia. Applicants can also contact UPEACE Somalia through the contact details provided by the institution for enquiries regarding admissions and scholarships. Conclusion The UPEACE Somalia 2026 admissions provide an opportunity for students and professionals from Somalia, East Africa and beyond to pursue postgraduate education in fields related to peace, governance, development, sustainability, humanitarian action, international law and environmental management. With Master’s and Doctoral programmes available online, the opportunity can provide greater flexibility for applicants seeking advanced academic qualifications while remaining in their home countries or continuing their professional activities. The availability of scholarships further increases the potential accessibility of these programmes, with the announcement indicating 30% scholarships for Master’s programmes, 50% scholarships for PhD programmes and 60% scholarships for UPEACE alumni. Interested applicants should review the programme-specific requirements and submit their applications before the 15 September 2026 scholarship deadline . Discover more on the OFY Webpage . title: Unearthodox Exploration Co-Lab 2027: Apply for CHF 10,000 Grant and 10-Month Incubation Programme
summary: Applications are now open for the Unearthodox Exploration Co-Lab 2027 , an alternative incubation programme supporting innovators and early-stage initiatives working to transform humanity’s relationship with nature and society. Organised by Unearthodox , the Exploration Co-Lab is designed for changemakers addressing complex environmental and social challenges at their root. The programme seeks applicants whose work goes beyond short-term or incremental solutions and instead explores new systems, worldviews, relationships, and pathways for a more just, vibrant, and regenerative future. Selected participants will receive CHF 10,000 in grant funding , a 10-month incubation journey , tailored non-financial support, peer learning, coaching, expert guidance, systems mapping, visibility opportunities, and access to a global community of innovators. The programme will run from 1 March to 31 December 2027 . Application deadline: 16 November 2026. What Is the Unearthodox Exploration Co-Lab? The Exploration Co-Lab is an alternative incubator for what Unearthodox describes as “edge-walkers”—innovators whose work challenges conventional approaches and does not fit easily into traditional categories. The programme is intended for people and initiatives exploring the deeper causes of nature-society challenges. Rather than focusing only on treating visible symptoms, the Co-Lab encourages participants to question the systems, assumptions, institutions, and relationships that have contributed to environmental and social problems. The programme is particularly interested in work that: Reimagines the relationship between humans and the natural world. Challenges dominant systems based on commodification or exploitation. Questions anthropocentric assumptions. Examines the effects of coloniality and unequal systems. Develops new ways of thinking about ecological and social wellbeing. Builds more regenerative, equitable, and community-centred futures. Creates stronger relationships with the more-than-human world. Explores new approaches to systems change and collective transformation. The Co-Lab recognises that deep systems change often requires time, experimentation, trust, reflection, relationships, and support for ideas that may initially appear unconventional or difficult to categorise. Key Details About the Exploration Co-Lab 2027 Programme: Unearthodox Exploration Co-Lab 2027 Organiser: Unearthodox Opportunity type: Incubator and grant-supported fellowship-style programme Grant funding: CHF 10,000 Programme duration: 10 months Programme dates: 1 March–31 December 2027 Application period: 15 September–16 November 2026 Application deadline: 16 November 2026 Format: Primarily online Working language: English Geographic scope: Global Target applicants: Early-stage initiatives and innovators working at the intersection of environmental and societal change What Does the Programme Offer? The Exploration Co-Lab combines financial support, learning, coaching, community, visibility, and strategic development. 1. CHF 10,000 in Grant Funding Selected initiatives will receive a grant of: CHF 10,000 The funding is intended to help participants move their initiatives forward. Applicants should be able to explain how the grant will contribute to the development, testing, deepening, or transformation of their work. The grant may help an initiative: Conduct further research. Test or refine a pilot. Engage communities. Develop new tools or approaches. Strengthen project implementation. Explore new pathways for systems change. Build partnerships. Develop a more sustainable operating model. Expand the initiative’s capacity to create impact. Applicants should connect their proposed use of funds to the stage and needs of their initiative. 2. A 10-Month Incubation Journey The programme offers a structured 10-month incubation journey beginning in March 2027 and ending in December 2027. Participants will join a cohort of changemakers in an online environment focused on: Systems transformation. Collective learning. Collaboration. Connection. Experimentation. Changemaker wellbeing. Strategic development. Regenerative approaches to impact. The incubation is designed to provide participants with space to think deeply, learn from others, and develop their work in a supportive environment. 3. Tailored Non-Financial Support Participants will have access to a shared pool of non-financial support estimated at up to: CHF 60,000 in value This support is tailored to the needs of the cohort and may include: Peer learning. Shared exploration. Individual coaching. Expert guidance. Systems mapping. Futures thinking. Strategic positioning. Regenerative approaches to defining and measuring success. The support is not necessarily provided as a cash award. Instead, it is intended to give participants access to knowledge, expertise, relationships, and tools that can help them develop their initiatives. 4. Peer Learning and Shared Exploration Participants will become part of an interdisciplinary cohort of innovators working on complex challenges. Peer learning may help participants: Exchange experiences. Learn from different approaches. Identify new possibilities. Reflect on challenges. Test assumptions. Build relationships with other changemakers. Discover potential collaborators. Develop a stronger understanding of systems change. The Co-Lab values shared learning and collective problem-solving rather than competition between participants. 5. Individualised Coaching and Expert Guidance The programme provides access to individualised coaching and expert guidance. This support may help participants clarify: Their initiative’s purpose. The systems they are trying to influence. Their theory of change. Their strategic priorities. Their approach to collaboration. Their methods for measuring progress. Their long-term sustainability needs. The specific support available may depend on the needs of each participant and the expertise within the programme’s wider network. 6. Systems Mapping and Futures Thinking Participants will have opportunities to explore practical approaches such as systems mapping and futures thinking . These approaches can help innovators understand: The relationships between different actors. The structures that maintain a problem. The assumptions underlying existing systems. Possible future scenarios. Points where change may be possible. The conditions required for an initiative to thrive. This is especially relevant for applicants whose work addresses complex challenges that cannot be solved through a single intervention. 7. Strategic Positioning The Co-Lab will also support participants in thinking about the strategic positioning of themselves and their initiatives. This may include clarifying: What makes the initiative distinctive. Which audiences and partners need to understand the work. How the initiative can communicate its purpose. What networks could support its development. How the initiative can become more visible, findable, and fundable. 8. Regenerative Approaches to Measuring Success Unearthodox encourages applicants and participants to think beyond conventional measures of growth and success. The programme includes support for regenerative approaches to defining and measuring success. This may involve considering: Ecological wellbeing. Community resilience. Relationships. Equity. Long-term systems change. Collective capacity. Quality of participation. The sustainability of the work itself. This approach recognises that meaningful change cannot always be captured through short-term numerical indicators alone. 9. Visibility and Amplification Selected initiatives will be showcased through Unearthodox’s communication channels. This may help participants become: More visible to relevant audiences. More discoverable by potential partners. More credible to prospective supporters. More connected to wider networks. More fundable over time. Visibility and amplification are intended to help promising initiatives gain recognition and access to further opportunities. 10. Global Community and Collaboration Participants will gain access to a global network of: Systems innovators. Mentors. Network weavers. Changemakers. Potential collaborators. People working on related environmental and social challenges. Unearthodox describes this community as a space for belonging, mutual support, deep allyship, and collaboration. Who Is the Exploration Co-Lab For? The Exploration Co-Lab is open to people who share a commitment to reimagining systems for a: Just future. Vibrant future. Regenerative future. The programme is intended for innovators who are willing to challenge conventional thinking and explore new possibilities with an engaged and interdisciplinary cohort. Applicants should value: Participation. Trust. Empathy. Critical thinking. Creative thinking. Collective learning. Community engagement. Long-term change. Collaboration across disciplines and backgrounds. The programme is particularly suitable for people who do not necessarily have a straightforward or conventional career or project journey, but who are actively working on meaningful environmental and societal transformation. Eligibility and Stage of Initiative Applicants should be working on an early-stage initiative at the intersection of environmental and societal change . The initiative does not need to be fully developed or have every detail resolved. However, applicants must be beyond the basic idea stage. Some groundwork should already exist, such as: Initial research. Early testing. A pilot project. Community engagement. An emerging intervention. A developing model or approach. Early evidence of a problem-solution relationship. A concept that exists only on paper, without any research, testing, engagement, or practical development, may not be suitable for this call. Initiative Development Stages Considered Unearthodox recognises that initiatives may be at different stages of development. Applicants may identify with one of the following phases. 1. Testing At the testing stage, an initiative may have limited resources and be exploring what works through direct engagement with: Communities. People affected by the issue. Local environments. Living systems. Relevant stakeholders. The focus is on learning, experimentation, and understanding whether the proposed approach is appropriate. 2. Proving At the proving stage, an initiative has a tangible proof of concept demonstrating that its central idea may work. The applicant may be seeking support to: Continue testing. Refine the approach. Improve implementation. Collect evidence. Build momentum. Strengthen the model. 3. Deepening At the deepening stage, the initiative has begun to demonstrate what it can make possible. The applicant may now be ready to: Explore new pathways. Adapt the approach. Deepen community relationships. Strengthen systems understanding. Develop more meaningful impact. Expand the depth rather than simply the size of the work. 4. Pivoting Some applicants may be leading more established initiatives that require a meaningful change in: Direction. Strategy. Approach. Operating model. Theory of change. Relationship with communities or ecosystems. The Co-Lab may be suitable for initiatives that need to rethink their existing model in response to new learning or changing conditions. 5. Other Development Stages Applicants who do not fit neatly into one of these categories are still encouraged to apply if their work aligns with the programme’s purpose. They should explain their current stage of activity and describe what kind of support would help the initiative move forward. Diversity, Inclusion, and Participation Unearthodox welcomes underrepresented voices from the global majority and historically excluded communities. The programme embraces diversity across: Age. Gender identity. Geographic location. Cultural background. Professional background. Lived experience. Social and community context. As a Swiss-founded organisation, Unearthodox also seeks to deepen exchange between Swiss-based innovators and innovators from other parts of the world working on regeneration. The organisation aims to include at least one Swiss-based initiative in each annual cohort. However, Swiss-based initiatives will be selected based on the strength and relevance of their work alongside other applicants. The programme does not indicate that applicants must belong to a particular race, ethnicity, gender, or nationality. Instead, it expresses a particular welcome toward underrepresented and historically excluded communities. Programme Language and Time-Zone Considerations All programme activities are conducted in: English Regular online group calls are scheduled within the time range of: UTC−6 to UTC+6 Applicants and participants located within these time zones may find it easier to participate synchronously in group sessions. People outside these time zones may still consider applying, but they should assess whether they can participate effectively in the scheduled online activities. What Counts as a Nature-Society Challenge? Unearthodox defines nature-society challenges as issues arising from the ways human societies and natural systems interact. These challenges may include: Climate change. Biodiversity loss. Habitat destruction. Environmental degradation. Unsustainable resource use. Human-centred systems that disregard other forms of life. Social inequalities connected to environmental systems. Extractive economic and institutional structures. Disconnection between people and the more-than-human world. The Co-Lab is interested in initiatives that explore new possibilities at this intersection and seek to create conditions in which both people and living systems can thrive. Questions Applicants Should Consider Applicants should reflect on the deeper purpose and potential of their work. Useful questions include: What future is the initiative helping to create? What kind of future is the initiative trying to move away from? How does the initiative encourage people to see, act, connect, or live differently in relation to the more-than-human world? How does the work challenge existing systems, assumptions, or norms? How could the initiative help all life on Earth thrive together? What conditions are needed for the work to flourish? What deeper purpose connects the applicant with others working on similar challenges? How are communities involved in shaping the work? What has already been tested, learned, or developed? What kind of support would make the greatest difference at this stage? These questions can help applicants determine whether their initiative aligns with the programme’s focus on deep systems change. Types of Work the Programme Is Looking For The Exploration Co-Lab does not appear to be restricted to one specific sector or discipline. Potentially relevant initiatives may work in areas such as: Environmental justice. Climate action. Biodiversity conservation. Regenerative agriculture. Ecological restoration. Community resilience. Alternative economic systems. Indigenous and traditional ecological knowledge. Environmental education. Sustainable livelihoods. Social innovation. More-than-human relationships. Systems transformation. Food systems. Urban ecology. Environmental governance. Community-led conservation. Post-growth approaches. New models of collective wellbeing. However, an initiative’s relevance will depend on whether it addresses the deeper relationship between nature and society and demonstrates a commitment to justice, regeneration, and systemic transformation. Work That May Not Align With the Call Unearthodox explains that the Exploration Co-Lab is not intended for projects that: Reinforce extractive or dominant systems. Prioritise profit, speed, or growth above purpose. Address only surface-level symptoms. Seek individual advantage without genuine collective learning. Lack meaningful interest in allyship. Focus exclusively on short-term outcomes without considering deeper conditions. Treat communities as passive recipients rather than active participants. This does not mean that every applicant must reject all existing institutions or economic activity. Rather, the programme seeks initiatives that critically examine harmful systems and work toward more equitable and regenerative alternatives. Application Timeline The 2027 Exploration Co-Lab follows the timeline below: Stage Date Applications open 15 September 2026 Application deadline 16 November 2026 Shortlisting and evaluation 17 November–11 December 2026 Applicant conversations/interviews 14–18 December 2026 Final selection with external jurors 5 January–4 February 2027 Participant notification and onboarding 5–28 February 2027 Incubation programme 1 March–31 December 2027 Applicants should submit their materials before the deadline and remain available for potential conversations or interviews during the stated selection period. Learn More HERE. How to Apply Interested applicants should begin by reviewing the official applicant information document. The document includes: Application form preview. Eligibility information. Evaluation criteria. Frequently asked questions. Terms and conditions. Guidance based on previous applications. Additional application tips. Applicants can access the Official Applicant Information Document . Applications can be submitted through the Unearthodox Exploration Co-Lab 2027 application portal . How to Prepare a Strong Application 1. Clearly Explain the Problem Describe the nature-society challenge your initiative addresses. Explain: Who or what is affected. Why the challenge exists. What systems or assumptions contribute to it. Why conventional solutions may be insufficient. Why the issue requires deeper transformation. 2. Demonstrate That You Are Beyond the Idea Stage Provide evidence of groundwork, such as: Research. Pilot activities. Community engagement. Early testing. Partnerships. Initial results. Existing prototypes. Practical experimentation. The initiative does not need to be fully mature, but the application should demonstrate that meaningful work has already begun. 3. Explain Your Approach to Systems Change Describe how your initiative seeks to influence underlying systems rather than only treating symptoms. You may discuss: Institutional structures. Cultural assumptions. Economic incentives. Power relationships. Environmental relationships. Community practices. Governance systems. Dominant narratives. Social norms. 4. Show Community Participation Explain how the people most affected by the issue participate in: Identifying the problem. Designing the solution. Making decisions. Implementing activities. Evaluating progress. Adapting the initiative. Community participation should be demonstrated through actual practices rather than presented only as a general principle. 5. Identify What You Need to Develop Be specific about the support your initiative needs. For example, you may need: Strategic guidance. Systems mapping. Research support. Community engagement resources. A new pilot. Partnership development. Coaching. A revised theory of change. New ways to measure impact. Time and space for reflection. 6. Explain How the CHF 10,000 Grant Will Be Used Provide a realistic explanation of how the grant will contribute to the initiative. Potential uses may include: Research and testing. Community activities. Materials. Travel connected to the project. Specialist support. Pilot implementation. Communications. Monitoring and learning. Project coordination. Applicants should ensure that proposed expenditure is directly connected to the initiative’s development and intended outcomes. 7. Demonstrate Openness to Collective Learning The Co-Lab is cohort-based. Applicants should show that they are willing to: Share learning. Receive feedback. Collaborate. Question assumptions. Learn from other disciplines. Participate in group activities. Contribute to a supportive community. 8. Consider Accessibility and Participation Since the programme operates online and uses English, applicants should consider their ability to participate in group sessions and complete programme activities. Those outside the UTC−6 to UTC+6 range should assess how they will manage time-zone differences. Application Deadline The application period runs from: 15 September 2026 to 16 November 2026 The official application deadline is: 16 November 2026 Applicants should not wait until the final day to submit. Reviewing the applicant information document and preparing a thoughtful application may require time, particularly for initiatives that need to gather evidence of community engagement, project development, and existing work. Contact Information For questions about the Exploration Co-Lab, applicants can contact: Email: colab@unearthodox.org For partnership-related enquiries, Unearthodox provides the following contact: sofia.papadakaki@unearthodox.org About Unearthodox Unearthodox is an organisation focused on supporting unconventional approaches to environmental and social transformation. Its work explores how innovation, relationships, systems change, regeneration, and collective learning can contribute to more just and sustainable futures. The Exploration Co-Lab is part of this wider approach. It seeks to create a supportive environment for innovators whose work may be difficult to place within traditional funding or incubation structures. Visit HERE to learn more about the Unearthodox Exploration Co-Lab, 2027. Conclusion The Unearthodox Exploration Co-Lab 2027 is an opportunity for innovators and early-stage initiatives working on the deeper relationship between nature and society. The programme offers a combination of CHF 10,000 in grant funding , a 10-month incubation journey , tailored coaching, expert guidance, peer learning, systems mapping, futures thinking, strategic positioning, visibility, and access to a global community of changemakers. It is particularly suited to applicants whose work goes beyond incremental environmental or social interventions and seeks to challenge underlying systems, assumptions, and relationships. Initiatives should already have some groundwork in place through research, testing, pilot activities, or community engagement. The programme welcomes applicants from diverse backgrounds and particularly encourages applications from underrepresented voices and historically excluded communities. Activities are conducted in English, with online group calls generally scheduled within UTC−6 to UTC+6. Applications are open from 15 September to 16 November 2026 . Interested applicants should review the official guidance, assess how their initiative aligns with the programme’s focus, and prepare a clear explanation of their work, community relevance, systems-change approach, development stage, and funding needs.
