title: Gilman-McCain Scholarship 2026: Apply for a $5,000 Study Abroad Scholarship for U.S. Military Family Dependents
summary: The John S. McCain International Scholarship for Military Families (Gilman-McCain Scholarship) is a U.S. government-funded scholarship opportunity designed to help eligible undergraduate students from U.S. military families participate in international education and internship experiences. The scholarship provides awards of up to $5,000 toward the costs associated with eligible credit-bearing study abroad programs and international internships. The program is particularly intended for children and spouses of active or activated U.S. military personnel who meet the scholarship s academic, financial-aid, program, citizenship, and travel-security requirements. The Fall 2026 Gilman-McCain Scholarship application is currently open , providing an opportunity for eligible students whose approved study abroad programs or international internships begin between December 1, 2026, and October 31, 2027 . About the Gilman-McCain Scholarship The Gilman-McCain Scholarship is a congressionally funded initiative administered through the Bureau of Educational and Cultural Affairs of the U.S. Department of State . It was established within the broader framework of the Benjamin A. Gilman International Scholarship Program and is named in honor of the late Senator John S. McCain of Arizona. The scholarship is intended to expand access to international educational opportunities for students from U.S. military families. Through financial support for eligible overseas study and internship programs, recipients can gain international exposure, develop professional and leadership skills, and broaden their understanding of different cultures and global issues. Unlike scholarships that are broadly available to undergraduate students, the Gilman-McCain Scholarship has a specific target population: eligible undergraduate children and spouses of active or activated U.S. military personnel . For the current academic year, the program offers 100 scholarships worth $5,000 each . What Does the Gilman-McCain Scholarship Fund? Successful applicants receive a $5,000 scholarship award that can be used toward the costs of an eligible credit-bearing study abroad or international internship program. The award is intended to help reduce the financial barriers associated with international education. Depending on the program and the student s circumstances, study abroad expenses can include various costs associated with participating in an overseas academic or internship experience. The scholarship is therefore particularly relevant to eligible students who have secured or are pursuing international programs but require additional financial support to participate. Fall 2026 Gilman-McCain Scholarship Application The Fall 2026 application cycle is open for eligible students whose study abroad programs or internships begin during the specified program period. Eligible programs for this cycle must begin between: December 1, 2026, and October 31, 2027 The cycle includes programs taking place during: Winter or January Term 2027 Spring 2027 Maymester 2027 Summer 2027 Fall 2027 Academic Year 2027–2028 Application Deadline The deadline for the Fall 2026 application is: Thursday, October 1, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. Pacific Time Applicants should also be aware that submitting the application is not the only deadline involved in the process. Their study abroad advisor must complete the required certification by: Thursday, October 8, 2026 Applicants should therefore begin the process early enough to allow their advisors and financial aid offices sufficient time to complete any required certifications. Who Can Apply for the Gilman-McCain Scholarship? The scholarship has specific eligibility requirements. Applicants must satisfy all applicable conditions to be considered. An applicant must be: 1. A U.S. Citizen or National Applicants must be citizens or nationals of the United States . This means that the scholarship is not a general international scholarship open to students from countries around the world. Its eligibility is specifically tied to U.S. citizenship or nationality as well as the other requirements of the program. 2. An Undergraduate Student Applicants must be undergraduate students in good standing at an accredited institution of higher education in the United States. Both two-year and four-year U.S. colleges and universities are included. Students should therefore be enrolled in an eligible undergraduate program at an accredited U.S. higher education institution when applying. 3. A Child or Spouse of Eligible U.S. Military Personnel A central requirement of the Gilman-McCain Scholarship is that the applicant must be a dependent child or spouse of active or activated United States military personnel at the time of application . Eligible military service categories include: Air Force Air Force Reserve Air National Guard Army Army National Guard Army Reserve Coast Guard Coast Guard Reserve Marine Corps Marine Corps Reserve Navy Navy Reserve Space Force NOAA Commissioned Corps U.S. Public Health Service Commissioned Corps Applicants are required to provide documentation confirming their dependent status and the qualifying military member s status. The program indicates that the DD1173 military identification form is used to confirm child or spousal dependent status and the active military status of the guardian or spouse. What If the Military Parent or Spouse Leaves Active Service Before the Study Abroad Program? An important feature of the eligibility rules is that the qualifying military status is considered at the time the student applies . Therefore, if a student s parent or spouse is an active military member when the student submits the application but is no longer active when the student eventually travels abroad, the student can still be eligible based on the stated program rules. This makes the timing of the military status particularly important when determining eligibility. Federal Financial Aid Requirement In addition to the military-family requirement, applicants must receive any type of Title IV federal financial aid during the application period or provide proof that they will receive Title IV federal financial aid during their study abroad program or internship. This requirement is broader than eligibility for a Federal Pell Grant. Students should therefore not assume that they are ineligible simply because they are not receiving a Pell Grant. The Gilman-McCain Scholarship specifically states that applicants may qualify through any type of Title IV federal financial aid , provided the applicable requirements are satisfied. Applicants should verify their federal financial aid status and provide the required information or documentation as part of the application process. Study Abroad or International Internship Requirement Applicants must be in the process of applying to, or already accepted into, a credit-bearing study abroad or internship program . The program must meet the scholarship s requirements, and proof of acceptance is required before the scholarship can be disbursed. This means that students should carefully examine their intended international program to make sure it qualifies before assuming that the scholarship can be used to finance it. Eligible applicants may use the scholarship for approved international education or internship experiences that are connected to academic credit. Travel Security Requirements The destination of the proposed international program is also an important part of eligibility. Applicants must be applying for a credit-bearing study abroad program in a country or location that has an overall Travel Advisory Level 1 or Level 2 under the U.S. Department of State s Travel Advisory System. However, students should not look only at the overall advisory level for a country. A country with an overall Level 1 or Level 2 rating may contain particular regions or locations designated as Level 3 or Level 4 . Gilman-McCain scholars cannot participate in programs located in areas designated at those higher advisory levels. In practical terms, applicants should carefully review the current travel advisory for both the country and the specific destination of their proposed program. The scholarship program also notes that the U.S. Department of State may request changes to a program s location when necessary during the application, selection, or program period. Awards are also subject to the availability of funding and the security situation in the destination country. Restrictions Relating to Certain Foreign Institutions There are additional restrictions concerning overseas institutions involved in the program. Gilman-McCain Scholars cannot participate in education abroad programs involving an overseas institution that appears on the Section 1286 National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) List of Foreign Institutions Engaging in Problematic Activities. The supplied program information notes that the annually updated list dated June 26, 2026 applies to programs in China. Students planning to study abroad should therefore check whether their proposed overseas institution is subject to this restriction before finalizing their plans. What Happens if a Program s Security Situation Changes? International travel conditions can change after an application has been submitted or even after an award has been made. The U.S. Department of State reserves the right to request changes to specific countries or areas when circumstances require it. The program also states that programs already underway may be suspended in consultation with the relevant U.S. Embassy if circumstances warrant such action. Consequently, receiving a scholarship does not eliminate the need for recipients to continue monitoring official travel and security guidance. How Many Scholarships Are Available? The Gilman-McCain Scholarship currently offers: 100 awards $5,000 per award Funding for eligible credit-bearing study abroad or international internship programs The number of available awards means that eligible applicants should pay close attention to the application requirements and selection process. How Are Applications Reviewed? Applications first undergo an eligibility review. During this stage, the program reviews whether applicants satisfy the required eligibility criteria, including documentation establishing their dependent relationship to an active military member. Complete and eligible applications then proceed to the selection process. The program states that eligible Gilman-McCain applications are reviewed by selection panels separate from other applicants . Applicants should therefore make sure that all required sections, certifications, documentation, and essays are completed accurately before the relevant deadlines. Gilman-McCain Scholarship Application Process Students interested in applying should approach the application as a multi-step process rather than waiting until the final day. Step 1: Review the Eligibility Requirements Before starting the application, confirm that you meet the core requirements relating to: U.S. citizenship or nationality Undergraduate enrollment Enrollment at an accredited U.S. institution Military dependent status Active or activated military service Title IV federal financial aid Credit-bearing study abroad or internship participation Destination travel-advisory requirements Step 2: Identify an Eligible International Program Applicants should identify a suitable credit-bearing study abroad or international internship program. If the applicant has not yet been accepted, they may still apply while in the process of applying to the program. However, proof of program acceptance is required before scholarship funds can be disbursed. Step 3: Prepare Military Dependent Documentation Eligible applicants should prepare the required documentation demonstrating their relationship to the active military member. The program specifically references the DD1173 Form as documentation confirming child or spouse dependent status and the active military member s status. Step 4: Confirm Financial Aid Eligibility Applicants should verify that they are receiving, or will receive during the relevant program period, an eligible form of Title IV federal financial aid . The program does not limit eligibility solely to Pell Grant recipients. Step 5: Complete the Online Application Applicants should complete the official Gilman-McCain Scholarship application through the online application system. Step 6: Obtain Advisor Certification Study abroad advisor certification is required for Gilman-McCain Scholarship applicants. Students should communicate with their relevant advisor early rather than waiting until after submitting the application, because the advisor certification has its own deadline. For the Fall 2026 cycle, the advisor certification deadline is October 8, 2026 . Application Deadline and Important Dates For students planning to apply during the current cycle, the major dates are: Stage Date Fall 2026 application Open Eligible program start period December 1, 2026 – October 31, 2027 Fall 2026 application deadline October 1, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. Pacific Time Advisor certification deadline October 8, 2026 Applicant notification December 2026 Students should pay attention to the time zone because the application deadline is stated in Pacific Time , not East Africa Time or another local time zone. Winter Gilman-McCain Scholarship Application Cycle Students whose programs fall within a later portion of the eligible period may also have another application opportunity. The Gilman-McCain Winter Application is scheduled to open in mid-November for applicants whose study abroad programs or internships begin between: February 1, 2027, and October 31, 2027 This cycle covers: Spring 2027 Maymester 2027 Summer 2027 Fall 2027 Academic Year 2027–2028 The Winter application deadline is: Thursday, January 7, 2027, at 11:59 p.m. Pacific Time The corresponding advisor certification deadline is: Thursday, January 14, 2027 Applicants for this cycle are expected to receive notification of their status in February 2027 . Can Veterans or Dependents of Veterans Apply? The Gilman-McCain Scholarship is specifically intended for dependents of active or activated U.S. military personnel during the application period. According to the program s FAQ, dependents of veterans who are no longer active do not qualify under the Gilman-McCain Scholarship s military eligibility requirement. Students who do not qualify for Gilman-McCain because of this requirement may wish to investigate the broader Gilman Program and other study abroad funding opportunities. Can Dependents of Reservists Apply? Yes, provided the applicable active-service and other scholarship requirements are met. The eligibility provisions encompass the relevant military reserve categories, including: Air Force Reserve Army Reserve Coast Guard Reserve Marine Corps Reserve Navy Reserve The program also includes the National Guard categories and other listed uniformed services. Applicants should nevertheless provide the required military documentation demonstrating qualifying status. Can a Student Receive Both the Gilman and Gilman-McCain Scholarships? A student who receives a Federal Pell Grant and is also a child or spouse dependent of an active military member may meet the eligibility requirements for both programs. However, the student cannot receive both scholarships. If the student qualifies for the Gilman-McCain Scholarship, the program states that they will no longer be considered for the regular Gilman Scholarship. Students who qualify for both should therefore follow the program s guidance concerning which application to complete. Can Gilman-McCain Applicants Apply for the Critical Need Language Award? Yes. A Gilman-McCain applicant who is studying a qualifying critical need language in one of the specified locations may also be eligible for the Critical Need Language Award. This provides an additional opportunity for eligible recipients whose international academic programs include qualifying language study. Is There an Application Fee? No. The Gilman-McCain Scholarship application is free to submit . Applicants should be cautious of anyone requesting payment in exchange for access to the scholarship application itself. Students should use the official Gilman application system and official program resources when submitting their applications. Important Considerations Before Applying Prospective applicants should carefully review several factors before submitting an application. Confirm Your Military Dependent Status The military-family component is fundamental to the scholarship. Make sure you have the appropriate documentation proving your relationship to the qualifying military member. Verify Your Federal Financial Aid Do not assume that the absence of a Pell Grant automatically makes you ineligible. The program accepts any type of Title IV federal financial aid , subject to its requirements. Check Your Study Destination Review the U.S. Department of State Travel Advisory for your intended destination, including any specific region or city-level restrictions. Confirm the Program Is Credit-Bearing The scholarship is designed for qualifying credit-bearing study abroad programs and international internships. Make sure your proposed experience meets the program s requirements. Start Advisor Certification Early Advisor certification has a separate deadline. Waiting until the last moment could create unnecessary problems if your advisor needs additional information or documentation. Check Overseas Institution Restrictions Students should verify that the overseas institution involved in their program does not fall under the applicable Section 1286 NDAA restrictions. How to Apply for the Gilman-McCain Scholarship Eligible students should complete their applications through the official Gilman-McCain online application system. Applicants can also review the official Gilman-McCain Scholarship information before submitting their application. APPLY HERE Who Qualifies for This Opportunity? Category of people: Undergraduate students from U.S. military families who meet the program s specific eligibility requirements. Academic qualification: Applicants must be undergraduate students in good standing at an accredited two-year or four-year U.S. institution of higher education. Citizenship: Applicants must be U.S. citizens or nationals . Military-family requirement: Applicants must be the child or spouse of active or activated U.S. military personnel during the time of application and must provide the required documentation. Financial-aid requirement: Applicants must receive any type of Title IV federal financial aid during the application period or provide proof that they will receive Title IV federal financial aid during the eligible study abroad program or internship. Program requirement: Applicants must be applying to, or accepted into, a qualifying credit-bearing study abroad or internship program . Geographic eligibility: This is not an open international scholarship for applicants from Africa, Asia, Europe, or other regions . Eligibility is specifically tied to U.S. citizenship or nationality, enrollment at an accredited U.S. institution, and the other program requirements. The international destination is where the qualifying study abroad or internship takes place and must satisfy the program s travel-security requirements. Race/ethnicity: The eligibility information provided does not identify a particular racial or ethnic group as an eligibility requirement . The key eligibility factors are U.S. citizenship or nationality, undergraduate enrollment, qualifying military-dependent status, Title IV federal financial aid, and an eligible international program. Visit HERE to learn more about the Gilman-McCain Scholarship 2026. Conclusion The Gilman-McCain Scholarship provides a significant source of financial assistance for eligible undergraduate children and spouses of active or activated U.S. military personnel who want to undertake credit-bearing study abroad or international internship experiences. With 100 awards of $5,000 each , the program can help eligible students address some of the financial challenges associated with participating in international education. However, applicants must satisfy several specific requirements, including U.S. citizenship or nationality, undergraduate enrollment at an accredited U.S. institution, qualifying military-dependent status, Title IV federal financial aid eligibility, and participation in an eligible credit-bearing international program. For the Fall 2026 cycle , applicants whose programs begin between December 1, 2026, and October 31, 2027 , must submit their applications by October 1, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. Pacific Time , while advisor certification is due October 8, 2026 . Students who meet the requirements should carefully review the official guidelines, prepare their documentation and program information early, and submit their applications through the official online system before the applicable deadline. title: YSEALI Academic Fellows Program 2027: Fully Funded Five-Week Exchange Programme in the United States
summary: The Young Southeast Asian Leaders Initiative Academic Fellows Program 2027 , commonly known as YSEALI AFP , is inviting eligible young leaders from Southeast Asia to apply for a fully funded academic exchange programme in the United States. Sponsored by the U.S. Department of State , funded by the U.S. Government, and administered by the Maureen and Mike Mansfield Center at the University of Montana , the programme is designed to strengthen leadership skills, encourage cross-cultural understanding, and build lasting connections between the United States and Southeast Asia. The five-week programme brings undergraduate students and recent graduates to a U.S. college or university for an intensive experience combining academic learning, leadership development, community service, field visits, cultural activities, and professional networking. The 2027 application cycle covers both the Spring 2027 and Fall 2027 cohorts . Interested applicants must submit their applications before the official deadline. Overview of the YSEALI Academic Fellows Program The Young Southeast Asian Leaders Initiative is a U.S. Government initiative that supports emerging leaders across Southeast Asia. Its Academic Fellows component focuses on young people who demonstrate leadership potential, community involvement, academic interests, and a commitment to strengthening relationships between Southeast Asia and the United States. The programme does not only focus on classroom learning. It provides participants with opportunities to: Explore important regional and global issues. Learn about U.S. society, institutions, culture, and values. Develop leadership and problem-solving skills. Engage in community service. Build relationships with fellow young leaders. Gain practical exposure through academic field experiences. Develop ideas that can benefit their communities after returning home. Establish long-term connections with U.S. participants and YSEALI alumni. The programme’s broader goal is to foster a network of young leaders who can collaborate across national borders to address shared challenges. Programme Details Programme name: Young Southeast Asian Leaders Initiative Academic Fellows Program Abbreviation: YSEALI AFP Programme year: 2027 Duration: Approximately five weeks Location: United States Format: In-person academic exchange Funding: Fully funded by the U.S. Government Host institutions: U.S. colleges and universities Application deadline: October 12, 2026, at 20:00 WIB Spring 2027 expected dates: April 1–May 5, 2027 Fall 2027 expected dates: September 16–October 20, 2027 Official application platform: Submittable The programme website states that there will be one application cycle for both the Spring and Fall 2027 cohorts. Applicants will not have a separate later opportunity to apply specifically for the Fall 2027 cohort. What Does the Fully Funded Programme Cover? Selected YSEALI Academic Fellows participate at no cost to themselves. According to the programme’s official FAQ, the U.S. Department of State covers costs associated with international travel, the visa, and basic living expenses in the United States. The programme’s funding and support include the following: 1. International Travel Support Selected Fellows receive support for international travel connected to the programme. Round-trip airfare is arranged for travel to the United States at the beginning of the programme and departure at the end. Participants should note that the programme does not permit fellows to extend their official travel dates for personal travel, family visits, or other private reasons. 2. Visa Support Selected participants receive assistance related to the U.S. J-1 exchange visitor visa process. The programme prepares the relevant documentation, including the DS-2019 form, which is used to begin the J-1 visa application process. The official programme information states that: Visa fees are covered or waived for selected programme participants. Applicants must be eligible to receive a U.S. J-1 visa. Participants must follow the instructions provided by the programme and the relevant U.S. Embassy or Consulate. Visa approval remains subject to the applicable procedures and requirements. Applicants do not need to have a valid passport at the time of application. However, selected Fellows must have a passport from an eligible YSEALI country before travelling to the United States. 3. Basic Living Costs The programme covers basic living expenses in the United States during the official exchange period. This allows selected participants to focus on academic activities, leadership development, community service, and cultural learning without paying programme participation fees. 4. Academic Learning and Leadership Development Fellows participate in an intensive academic residency at a U.S. university or college. The academic component introduces participants to relevant themes, U.S. institutions, policy approaches, and practical examples connected to their selected area of interest. 5. Community Service Activities Community service is an important part of the programme. Fellows participate in activities that encourage them to engage with local communities, understand social issues, and explore how civic participation can contribute to positive change. 6. Academic Field Experience The programme includes academic field experiences that allow participants to connect classroom discussions with real-world institutions, organizations, communities, and initiatives. These experiences are intended to broaden participants’ understanding of the United States and demonstrate how different sectors address social, economic, environmental, and security-related challenges. 7. Closing Workshop The five-week programme concludes with a closing workshop. This provides Fellows with an opportunity to reflect on what they have learned, share experiences, discuss future plans, and consider how they can apply their knowledge after returning home. 8. Cross-Cultural Networking Participants meet other young leaders from Southeast Asia and interact with U.S. citizens through the programme’s activities and reciprocal exchange component. These relationships can become valuable sources of collaboration, professional support, and cross-border learning. YSEALI Academic Fellowship Themes Applicants can express interest in one or more of the programme’s four major themes. The official programme website identifies the following areas: 1. Liberty and Freedom The Liberty and Freedom theme examines ideas connected to freedom of speech, liberty, self-governance, civic engagement, public advocacy, and individual rights. Participants may explore: Freedom of speech and expression. Civic participation. Public advocacy campaigns. Self-governance. The relationship between individual rights and social development. How citizens and groups have influenced U.S. history, government, and society. The role of open debate in innovation and public life. The theme also considers how liberty and civic freedoms relate to economic stability and societal development. 2. Natural Resources The Natural Resources theme explores the management, protection, and sustainable use of natural resources. It examines how agriculture, fisheries, energy, minerals, water, and other resources affect economic development and community well-being. Possible topics include: Agriculture and sustainable farming. Fisheries management. Energy security. Critical minerals. Supply chain resilience. Natural disaster preparedness. Mining and rare earth minerals. Water and waste management. Environmental sustainability. The relationship between natural resources and economic prosperity. This theme may be particularly relevant to applicants interested in environmental policy, climate resilience, agriculture, natural resource governance, sustainability, or community development. 3. Economic Prosperity The Economic Prosperity theme focuses on the systems, institutions, and practices that contribute to economic growth and opportunity. Topics may include: Business models. Entrepreneurship. Technological innovation. Labour market practices. Monetary policy. Financial literacy. Investment and fundraising. Organizational development. Strategic business planning. Corporate governance. Supply chain management. Strategic trade policies. Technology and artificial intelligence frameworks. Regulation and economic development. Applicants with interests in entrepreneurship, business, economics, finance, innovation, employment, technology, or inclusive economic growth may find this theme relevant. 4. Peace and Security The Peace and Security theme explores policies, institutions, and practices related to local, regional, and international peace and security. Potential topics include: Peacebuilding and conflict prevention. Public policy and peacemaking. Disaster preparedness and response. Cybersecurity. Public health security. Human trafficking. Drug trafficking. Transnational crime. Online scams. Border security. Regional and international cooperation. The theme may appeal to students and young professionals interested in peacebuilding, international relations, public policy, security studies, governance, disaster management, public health, or human rights. Applicants who are interested in more than one theme may be asked to rank their preferences in the application. However, selected Fellows will be assigned to a theme, and applicants cannot request a specific U.S. institute. Who Can Apply for the YSEALI Academic Fellows Program? The programme has specific eligibility requirements. Applicants should carefully review each condition before beginning their application. Age Requirement Applicants must generally be between 18 and 25 years old by October 12, 2026 , which is the application deadline. The programme notes that exceptional applicants over the age of 25 may be considered if they meet all other eligibility requirements. Applicants who are younger than 18 by the application deadline are not eligible, even if they will turn 18 before the programme begins. Citizenship Requirement Applicants must be citizens of one of the following eligible countries: Brunei Cambodia Indonesia Malaysia Philippines Singapore Thailand Timor-Leste Vietnam For the 2027 U.S.-based Academic Fellows Program, citizens of Myanmar and Laos are not eligible because of current visa restrictions. This restriction is based on citizenship and does not change based on the applicant’s country of residence. Residency Requirement Applicants must also be physically residing in an ASEAN member state as of October 12, 2026 , and must remain resident in an ASEAN member state through the start of their selected fellowship. Being a citizen of an eligible country is therefore not sufficient by itself. Applicants must meet both the citizenship and residency requirements. Academic Requirement Applicants must meet one of the following academic conditions: Be enrolled as a full-time undergraduate student. Be enrolled as a part-time undergraduate student. Be enrolled as a graduate student. Have graduated with an undergraduate degree within the last four years. The programme is intended for young people who are at the beginning stages of their academic, professional, or leadership careers. English-Language Requirement The fellowship is conducted entirely in English. Applicants must be proficient in: Reading English. Writing English. Speaking English. Applications must also be submitted in English. Applications submitted in another language will not be evaluated. Applicants who are deaf should be proficient in American Sign Language, according to the programme’s FAQ. U.S. Citizenship and Residency Restriction Applicants must not be: U.S. citizens. U.S. permanent residents. Green card holders. This restriction also applies to dual citizens who hold U.S. citizenship or permanent residency. Previous YSEALI Participation Applicants must not be alumni of the YSEALI Academic Fellows Program. Previous participation in the Academic Fellows programme makes an applicant ineligible for this particular opportunity. U.S. Government Employment Restriction Applicants must not be employees of the U.S. Government or immediate family members of U.S. Government employees. J-1 Visa Eligibility Applicants must be eligible to receive a U.S. J-1 visa. Selected participants will be guided through the relevant visa documentation and application process. Desired Qualifications Meeting the technical eligibility requirements does not automatically guarantee selection. The programme also identifies qualities and experiences that can strengthen an application. Strong applicants are expected to demonstrate some combination of the following: 1. Interest in a Fellowship Theme Applicants should demonstrate interest, knowledge, or relevant experience connected to one or more of the four fellowship themes: Liberty and Freedom. Natural Resources. Economic Prosperity. Peace and Security. This interest may be demonstrated through academic work, professional experience, volunteering, community service, student leadership, research, advocacy, entrepreneurship, or other relevant activities. 2. Leadership Potential Applicants should demonstrate leadership qualities and the potential to contribute positively to their university, workplace, organization, or community. Leadership does not necessarily mean holding a formal title. It may include: Organizing a community initiative. Leading a student association. Coordinating volunteers. Supporting a social enterprise. Conducting community research. Advocating for a public issue. Developing a local solution to a shared challenge. Mentoring other young people. Participating in civic or development activities. 3. Interest in the United States and Southeast Asia Applicants should express a genuine interest in learning about the United States and building relationships between the United States and Southeast Asia. The programme seeks participants who are open to cross-cultural learning and willing to engage respectfully with people from different backgrounds. 4. Commitment to Full Participation The YSEALI Academic Fellows Program is intensive. Selected Fellows must be prepared to participate fully in: Academic sessions. Community service. Field experiences. Workshops. Cultural activities. Site visits. Networking activities. Other scheduled programme components. The official FAQ states that Fellows cannot take time off for personal travel, schoolwork, employment, or other private matters during the programme. Full participation is required. 5. Commitment to Return Home Applicants should demonstrate a commitment to returning to their home country after the programme and applying the leadership skills, knowledge, and relationships gained through the fellowship. Applicants should be able to explain how the experience may benefit: Their local community. Their country. Southeast Asia. Their professional or academic field. Cross-border cooperation. Relationships between Southeast Asia and the United States. 6. Limited Prior U.S. Experience The programme particularly encourages applicants who have little or no prior study or travel experience in the United States. This does not mean that every applicant with previous U.S. experience is automatically disqualified. However, applicants with limited prior exposure to the United States may align more closely with this desired qualification. Programme Structure and Participant Experience The YSEALI Academic Fellows Program combines several components rather than relying exclusively on academic lectures. A typical fellowship experience includes: Academic residency: Fellows study their selected theme at a U.S. host institution. Community service: Participants engage in activities that connect academic learning with community needs. Academic field experience: Fellows visit or interact with institutions and organizations relevant to the programme theme. Cultural learning: Participants gain a deeper understanding of U.S. society, culture, history, and institutions. Leadership development: Fellows strengthen communication, collaboration, critical thinking, and problem-solving skills. Closing workshop: Participants reflect on their learning and consider future applications. Reciprocal exchange component: The programme includes a component through which Americans travel to Southeast Asia, supporting continued cross-cultural engagement. The programme is designed to encourage relationships that continue beyond the five-week exchange. Important Information About Travel and Participation Applicants should understand that the fellowship is a structured exchange programme rather than a general tourism or personal travel opportunity. Selected Fellows are expected to: Attend all required activities. Participate fully in academic and cultural sessions. Follow programme rules and travel arrangements. Travel on the dates arranged by the programme. Remain engaged throughout the official fellowship period. Return home at the end of the programme. The programme does not permit participants to bring family members to the United States as part of the fellowship. Personal travel extensions are also not permitted under the programme’s stated rules. Learn More HERE. Application Deadline The application deadline for the 2027 YSEALI Academic Fellows Program is: October 12, 2026, at 20:00 WIB Applicants should confirm the equivalent deadline in their local time zone and avoid waiting until the final hours to submit their application. The programme does not offer extensions after the deadline. Applicants should also note that submissions are final and cannot be edited after they have been submitted. How to Apply Interested applicants should follow these steps: Step 1: Review the Eligibility Requirements Confirm that you meet the programme’s age, citizenship, residency, academic, English-language, and visa requirements. Step 2: Review the Fellowship Themes Read about the four available themes and identify the areas that best match your academic interests, leadership experience, professional goals, or community work. Step 3: Prepare Your Application Information Prepare clear information about: Your academic background. Your community or leadership experience. Your professional interests. Your interest in the selected fellowship themes. Your interest in the United States and Southeast Asia. Your plans after completing the programme. How you intend to apply the fellowship experience in your community. Step 4: Submit the Online Application Applications must be submitted through the official Submittable application platform. The programme states that only applications submitted through the official online platform will be considered. A downloadable application form may be available for reference, but it is not a substitute for the online submission. Step 5: Submit Before the Deadline Complete and review the application carefully before submitting it by October 12, 2026, at 20:00 WIB . Get the Application Information HERE and Apply HERE . Application Tips Applicants can improve the clarity and strength of their applications by following these recommendations: Connect Your Experience to a Theme Do not simply state that you are interested in a theme. Explain how your studies, work, volunteering, research, or community involvement connect to it. For example, an applicant interested in Natural Resources could discuss experience in climate action, environmental education, sustainable agriculture, water management, or community conservation. Demonstrate Leadership with Evidence Use specific examples of what you have done. Explain: The challenge you identified. The action you took. The people or groups you worked with. The outcome of your efforts. What you learned from the experience. Explain Your Community Impact The programme values applicants who intend to apply their learning after returning home. Describe a realistic way you could use the knowledge, networks, or skills gained during the fellowship. Show Cross-Cultural Openness Explain how you would contribute to and learn from a diverse group of participants. Avoid presenting the exchange only as an opportunity for personal travel or career advancement. Review Eligibility Carefully Pay close attention to the citizenship and residency requirements. Applicants must be both citizens of an eligible country and residents of an ASEAN member state under the programme’s definition. Proofread Before Submission Applications must be submitted in English, and submissions are final. Check your responses for clarity, accuracy, grammar, and completeness before submitting. Official Application and Programme Links Official programme website: YSEALI Academic Fellows Program Application information and online application: Apply for YSEALI Academic Fellows Program Fellowship themes: YSEALI Institute Themes Frequently asked questions: YSEALI AFP FAQ Programme contact: ysealiafp@umontana.edu Conclusion The YSEALI Academic Fellows Program 2027 offers eligible young leaders from Southeast Asia an opportunity to participate in a fully funded, five-week academic and cultural exchange in the United States. Through academic study, community service, field experiences, leadership development, and cross-cultural networking, the programme seeks to prepare participants to contribute to their communities and strengthen relationships across Southeast Asia and the United States. Applicants should carefully review the eligibility requirements, identify the fellowship theme that best matches their experience, prepare thoughtful responses, and submit their applications before the October 12, 2026, at 20:00 WIB deadline. Because the programme covers both Spring and Fall 2027 cohorts in one application cycle, eligible applicants should not wait for a later Fall 2027 call before applying. title: Leibniz Summer Fellowships 2027 in Germany: International Postdoctoral Researchers Can Receive €3,000 Per Month for Contemporary History Research
summary: International historians and postdoctoral researchers specializing in twentieth-century German, European, or Eastern European history have an opportunity to spend two months conducting independent research in Germany through the Leibniz Summer Fellowships 2027 at the Leibniz Centre for Contemporary History Potsdam (Leibniz-Zentrum für Zeithistorische Forschung Potsdam – ZZF) . For the 2027 fellowship cycle, ZZF is inviting applications for two Leibniz Summer Fellowships focused on German and/or European, including Eastern European, History in the Twentieth Century . The program is specifically intended for international scholars who already hold a doctoral degree and are residing outside Germany when they apply. Successful fellows will spend two consecutive months in Berlin or Potsdam between April and October 2027 . Each fellow will receive a monthly grant of €3,000 , meaning that a two-month fellowship provides €6,000 in total grant support. The funding is intended to cover the fellow s living costs, travel and appropriate insurance during the fellowship period. The application deadline is November 30, 2026 . About the Leibniz Summer Fellowships 2027 The Leibniz Summer Fellowship is a research residency offered by the Leibniz Centre for Contemporary History Potsdam for established international scholars working in areas relevant to twentieth-century German and European history. The program combines two important elements: independent scholarly research and active participation in the intellectual life of ZZF. Rather than requiring fellows to work on a predetermined institutional project, ZZF allows successful applicants to continue research based on their own scholarly interests. Preference, however, is given to proposals that connect with one or more of the Centre s existing research departments. This approach makes the fellowship particularly attractive to postdoctoral historians who already have a developed research agenda and would benefit from access to German academic networks, historical resources and interaction with specialists working on related themes. Host Institution: Leibniz Centre for Contemporary History Potsdam The Leibniz Centre for Contemporary History Potsdam , commonly known as ZZF, is a major German research institute specializing in twentieth-century contemporary history and its connections with the present. Its work places particular emphasis on German and European social history after 1945 while situating those developments within broader international contexts. In addition to fundamental historical research, ZZF is involved in research infrastructure, digital knowledge transfer and cooperation with universities and research institutions in Germany and abroad. ZZF is a member of the Leibniz Association , one of Germany s major networks of non-university research institutions. The Centre has held Leibniz Association membership since 2009 and receives institutional support from both federal and state-level public funding. The institute also has an extensive international academic orientation, including cooperation with universities and research organizations as well as a visiting-researcher program. These connections help make the fellowship more than simply a short period of individual archival or library research. Two Fellowships Available for 2027 ZZF has announced two positions under the 2027 Leibniz Summer Fellowship program. The thematic field is: German and/or European, including Eastern European, History in the Twentieth Century This is broad enough to accommodate scholars working across multiple subfields of contemporary history, provided that their research has a substantive connection to German or European twentieth-century history. The opportunity is intended for international postdoctoral researchers rather than doctoral students or applicants who have not yet completed their doctorate. Fellowship Duration Each fellowship lasts for: Two consecutive months The research stay must take place between: April and October 2027 Successful candidates are expected to live in either Berlin or Potsdam, Germany , throughout their two-month fellowship period. Applicants should therefore consider their availability carefully before applying and identify a feasible two-month period within the April-to-October window. The requirement to remain locally based is important because the program is designed around participation in ZZF s academic environment rather than functioning as a remote research grant. Financial Support: €3,000 Per Month One of the major features of the Leibniz Summer Fellowship is its financial support. Each successful fellow receives: €3,000 per month Because the fellowship runs for two months, the total fellowship grant amounts to: €6,000 for the full two-month period ZZF states that this funding is expected to cover costs associated with the fellowship, including: Living expenses Travel expenses Appropriate insurance Applicants should understand that these costs are expected to be met from the €3,000 monthly fellowship payment rather than assuming that accommodation, flights or insurance will automatically be paid separately by the institution. Researchers considering the fellowship should therefore prepare an estimated budget covering transportation to Germany, temporary accommodation in Berlin or Potsdam, local transportation, meals, insurance and other personal expenses. Research Facilities Provided by ZZF In addition to the financial grant, fellows receive access to institutional research infrastructure. ZZF states that fellowship recipients will be provided with facilities including: Office space Computer access Other relevant institutional facilities These resources are designed to allow fellows to work from the Centre and participate meaningfully in its research community. This is particularly valuable for international researchers who want more than financial support and instead seek an immersive period within a specialist academic environment. Access to an Important Contemporary History Library Research fellows can also benefit from ZZF s specialist library. The ZZF library concentrates on German and European contemporary history after 1945 and includes material covering social and economic history, political and cultural history, media history, and the history of German division and reunification. Its catalogue also incorporates electronic and audiovisual resources, journal holdings and thousands of indexed academic articles. For scholars whose work relies on German-language scholarship or European contemporary history literature, proximity to such a specialized research collection can considerably strengthen a short research stay. ZZF s Main Research Departments Applicants have considerable freedom to pursue their own research, but there is a strategic advantage in demonstrating how a proposed project connects with ZZF s institutional expertise. The Centre s academic research is structured around five major research areas: Communism and Society Knowledge – Economy – Politics Media and Information Society Regimes of the Social Sphere Globalizations in a Divided World ZZF s overall research agenda covers twentieth-century German and European contemporary history from political, social, cultural, economic, media and transnational perspectives. Applicants should therefore study these departments before preparing their project proposal and identify where their own work has an intellectual connection with ZZF researchers. Research on Communism, Eastern Europe and Post-Communist Transformation Scholars specializing in Eastern European history may find the fellowship particularly relevant. For example, ZZF s Communism and Society department examines governance and social practices in the German Democratic Republic and Central and Eastern Europe. Its research also addresses transformations surrounding and extending beyond the political changes of 1989–1991, along with issues including violence, civil society and social developments in late and post-communist societies. This institutional expertise helps explain why the fellowship announcement explicitly includes Eastern European history within its thematic scope. Global and Transnational Perspectives The Centre s work is not limited to national German history. Its research also examines how German and European societies interacted with wider global transformations, including the Cold War, decolonization, changing international orders and transnational connections. ZZF s work on globalization examines how European societies both influenced and were influenced by international structures and cross-border developments. Applicants whose projects use comparative, transnational or global-history approaches may therefore find relevant intellectual connections at the Centre. Who Is Eligible for the Leibniz Summer Fellowships? Eligibility is comparatively straightforward but academically demanding. Applicants must meet the following central conditions: Hold a doctoral degree at the time the application is submitted Have postdoctoral standing Demonstrate an outstanding academic record Be an international applicant Reside outside Germany at the time of application Propose research relevant to twentieth-century German and/or European history, including Eastern European history ZZF explicitly defines the international character of the fellowship in terms of residence: applicants should be based outside Germany. This is therefore not a fellowship for applicants who are still completing their PhD or expect to receive the doctorate only after submitting the application. Do You Need to Be a German Citizen? No nationality requirement restricting the fellowship to German citizens is stated. In fact, the fellowship is designed for international researchers residing outside Germany . This means applicants from Africa, Asia, Europe outside Germany, North America, South America, Oceania and other regions may potentially apply, provided they meet the academic and residency requirements and their proposed research fits the fellowship s scholarly field. Nationality and residence should not, however, be confused. The explicit requirement concerns being an international applicant residing outside Germany at application stage. What Academic Background Is Required? This is an advanced research fellowship rather than a student scholarship. A completed doctoral degree is mandatory . The official call additionally emphasizes postdoctoral standing and a strong academic record. Accordingly, the fellowship is most appropriate for researchers such as: Postdoctoral scholars University lecturers Academic historians Research fellows Early- or mid-career researchers with completed PhDs Independent scholars with an established academic record, provided they satisfy the formal requirements The strongest applicants are likely to have a clearly defined research agenda, publications or other evidence of scholarly achievement and a project that can make productive use of a two-month stay at ZZF. Research Project Requirements Applicants are not required to join a predetermined research project. Instead, fellows can pursue their own individual research interests. However, ZZF specifically indicates that preference will be given to applicants whose projects relate to one or more of its research departments. Applicants should therefore avoid presenting the proposed project as completely isolated from the host institution. A strong proposal should explain why conducting the research specifically at ZZF would be useful. Relevant questions to address when developing the proposal include: How does the project relate to contemporary German or European history? Does it engage with Eastern European history where relevant? Which ZZF department has the strongest connection with the project? Which methodological or thematic conversations at ZZF could benefit the research? What specific progress can realistically be achieved within two months? Why is residence in Berlin or Potsdam valuable for the project? What scholarly output may result from the fellowship? These are strategic application considerations rather than additional formal requirements published by ZZF. Integration Into ZZF s Academic Community Successful applicants will not simply receive funding and work independently. Each fellow will be affiliated with one of ZZF s research departments. Fellows will be able to participate in departmental academic activities and will also be expected to present their research project through the institute s research seminar. This makes communication skills and willingness to engage academically with other researchers important aspects of the fellowship experience. Applicants should therefore approach the program as both an individual research residency and an academic-exchange opportunity. Required Application Documents The application package consists of four main documents: Letter of Interest Curriculum Vitae List of Publications Research Project Proposal of no more than 1,500 words All documents must be combined into one PDF attachment and submitted electronically. The application may be prepared in either: English or German This allows international scholars who do not write academically in German to apply in English. No Recommendation Letter Required An important feature of the application process is that applicants do not need to submit a letter of recommendation . This simplifies the application process because candidates do not have to arrange an external academic referee or wait for recommendation letters before the deadline. The application will therefore depend heavily on the quality of the applicant s own academic record, CV, publication record, statement of interest and research proposal. How to Prepare the 1,500-Word Project Proposal The project proposal is likely to be one of the most important components of the application. Because it cannot exceed 1,500 words , applicants should make every section purposeful. A useful structure could include: Research Title Use a precise academic title reflecting the central historical question or argument. Research Background Briefly explain the historical issue, scholarly debate or research gap that motivates the project. Research Questions State clearly what the project seeks to investigate. Sources and Methodology Identify the types of sources, archives, publications or methodological approaches that will be used. Contribution to Scholarship Explain what new knowledge, argument or perspective the project could add to existing research. Relevance to ZZF Identify the ZZF department or research themes that connect most directly with the project. Fellowship Work Plan Explain what can realistically be accomplished during the two-month stay. This suggested structure is application guidance rather than a format mandated by the official call. How to Prepare the Letter of Interest The letter of interest should complement rather than duplicate the research proposal. Applicants can use it to explain: Their current academic position and research trajectory Why they are applying for the Leibniz Summer Fellowship Why ZZF is an appropriate host institution What they hope to achieve during the residency How interaction with the Centre s scholars may support the project How the fellowship fits into their broader academic development Candidates should keep the letter focused and professional. Preparing the Publication List Because ZZF asks applicants to demonstrate a strong academic record, the publication list provides important evidence of scholarly development. Depending on the applicant s career stage, it may include: Peer-reviewed journal articles Academic books or monographs Edited volumes Book chapters Published research reports Relevant scholarly publications Applicants should provide complete bibliographical information and organize their publications clearly. How to Submit the Application Applications must be submitted electronically by email. The official fellowship email address is: fellowships@zzf-potsdam.de All required documents should be consolidated into one PDF attachment . ZZF does not request a recommendation letter. Applicants should carefully check that all four required components are included before sending the application. Application Deadline The final deadline is: November 30, 2026 Applications should be completed and submitted by this date. ZZF states that fellowship decisions will be communicated no later than: December 31, 2026 . This relatively short decision period gives successful applicants several months to organize travel, accommodation, insurance and research arrangements before the fellowship period begins in April 2027. Key Dates at a Glance Stage Date / Period Application deadline November 30, 2026 Fellowship decisions By December 31, 2026 Fellowship period Two consecutive months Eligible residency window April–October 2027 Location Berlin or Potsdam, Germany Monthly fellowship grant €3,000 Total for two months €6,000 These dates and funding conditions are stated in the official 2027 fellowship announcement. Why Researchers Should Consider This Opportunity For eligible historians, the Leibniz Summer Fellowship offers several advantages in one program. It provides direct financial support, a temporary institutional base in Germany, access to academic facilities and the opportunity to interact with scholars specializing in contemporary European history. The fellowship may be particularly useful for researchers who are: Developing an article or book project on twentieth-century Europe Conducting postdoctoral research involving Germany Working on Central or Eastern European contemporary history Expanding a project into comparative or transnational European history Seeking intellectual exchange with German-based scholars Planning research that benefits from spending time in Berlin or Potsdam ZZF s international cooperation, specialist research departments and contemporary-history resources provide an academic environment particularly relevant to these objectives. Important Points to Remember Before Applying Applicants should pay particular attention to several requirements. First, a doctorate must already have been completed when the application is submitted . Second, this call is intended for international applicants residing outside Germany . Third, although applicants can propose their own research, aligning the proposal with ZZF s research profile can strengthen its institutional relevance. Fourth, the fellowship lasts exactly two consecutive months and fellows must reside in Berlin or Potsdam during that period. Finally, the €3,000 monthly payment is intended to cover multiple types of expenditure, including living, travel and insurance costs. Applicants should therefore plan their budget accordingly. Conclusion The Leibniz Summer Fellowships 2027 at the Leibniz Centre for Contemporary History Potsdam offer an excellent short-term research opportunity for international postdoctoral historians interested in twentieth-century German, European or Eastern European history. With two fellowships available , a €3,000 monthly grant , access to ZZF s academic facilities and specialist research environment, and the opportunity to participate directly in departmental and seminar activities, the program provides both financial support and meaningful scholarly engagement. Applicants must already hold a doctorate, demonstrate a strong academic record and reside outside Germany when applying. Successful researchers will spend two consecutive months in Berlin or Potsdam sometime between April and October 2027. The most important date to remember is November 30, 2026 , when applications close. Candidates should prepare a letter of interest, CV, publication list and a research proposal of no more than 1,500 words, combine everything into one PDF and submit it to the official fellowship email address.
