title: Bank of America Campus Programs 2026: Internships, Analyst and Associate Opportunities for University Students
summary: University students and recent graduates seeking to begin a career with one of the world s leading financial institutions can explore a wide range of early-career opportunities through the Bank of America Campus Experience . Bank of America s campus recruitment platform is designed to help university and advanced-degree students gain practical professional experience, build industry knowledge, develop technical and interpersonal skills, and potentially transition into full-time careers with the organization. Rather than representing one single program, the Bank of America Campus Experience brings together a range of opportunities, including summer internships, pre-internship programs, industrial placements, analyst positions, associate opportunities and other early-career pathways across different business divisions and geographical regions. Students interested in banking, finance, investment banking, technology, operations, corporate functions, wealth management and related areas can explore opportunities based on their academic background, career interests and location. Bank of America states that candidates for its campus opportunities must generally be currently enrolled in a college, university or advanced-degree program . Individual programs may have additional academic, technical, language, graduation-date or work-authorization requirements. About the Bank of America Campus Experience The Bank of America Campus Experience is designed to provide students and emerging professionals with exposure to the bank s workplace, employees, business operations and professional development resources. Successful applicants can gain more than conventional classroom learning. Depending on the program, participants may receive structured training, practical assignments, professional mentorship, networking opportunities and exposure to employees working across different areas of Bank of America. The bank describes its campus experience as an environment where motivated and ambitious students can develop their skills while gaining practical insight into professional life. Bank of America highlights several important elements of the campus experience, including mentorship, training, networking, orientation, community-building opportunities, professional events and interaction with other early-career participants. Why Students May Consider Bank of America Campus Opportunities Starting a professional career can be challenging for university students because employers frequently look for candidates who can combine academic knowledge with practical workplace skills. Bank of America s student programs are structured to help bridge this gap. Through its campus programs, students may have opportunities to understand how a major global financial institution operates while learning directly from professionals in their chosen field. Participants can potentially develop experience in areas such as financial services, technology, business operations, investment banking, corporate functions, risk, client services and wealth management. For students who eventually want to join Bank of America on a full-time basis, internships may also represent an important route into the company s graduate recruitment pipeline. Bank of America states that its summer internship class is a primary source of candidates for its full-time campus programs. What Does the Bank of America Campus Experience Offer? 1. Professional Mentorship Participants may receive guidance from experienced professionals working in their areas of interest. This can help students better understand professional expectations, career development and the practical application of concepts they have studied at university. Mentorship can be particularly valuable for individuals entering industries such as investment banking, technology, financial markets and corporate services, where learning directly from experienced professionals can complement academic study. 2. Training and Skills Development Bank of America emphasizes professional training as an important part of its student experience. Participants can develop skills extending beyond what they have learned in university. Depending on the program and business area, this may involve learning about financial products, technology systems, business processes, client relationships, analytical work, teamwork and professional communication. 3. Networking Opportunities Campus participants can interact with employees and other students across Bank of America. Networking can help students better understand different career paths and develop professional relationships with people from various teams and divisions. Participants may also interact with other interns or members of their program cohort. 4. Orientation and Onboarding Students joining Bank of America programs may receive structured onboarding designed to introduce them to the organization, its working environment and their responsibilities. A well-developed orientation process can help participants adjust more quickly when moving from an academic environment into a professional workplace. 5. Culture and Community The campus experience also gives participants opportunities to build relationships with other students entering the organization. Cohort-based programs can allow participants to share experiences, learn collaboratively and develop professional networks that may continue beyond the duration of the program. 6. Professional and Social Events Depending on the program and location, participants may have access to activities specifically designed for interns and early-career professionals. These can complement formal work experience by providing additional opportunities for engagement with colleagues and the broader organization. Bank of America Internship Opportunities Internships represent one of the main pathways available through Bank of America s campus recruitment system. Summer internships typically target students in the penultimate year of university who expect to begin full-time employment after completing their degree. Bank of America states that these internships typically last approximately 10 weeks , although program length can differ by region and specific opportunity. Interns may work directly within a Bank of America business team rather than participating only in classroom-based activities. This can enable participants to experience actual working conditions, contribute to projects, receive feedback and better understand whether a specific career path suits their professional ambitions. In the Asia-Pacific region, Bank of America states that summer internships usually run for approximately eight to ten weeks. Timing differs by market: internships in India generally take place between April and May, while many other APAC locations run summer internships between June and August. Australia follows a different schedule, with summer internships typically lasting about 11 weeks between November and February. Full-Time Analyst Opportunities Bank of America s full-time analyst programs are designed primarily for students approaching university graduation and preparing to begin full-time professional employment. Analyst positions are generally associated with candidates studying toward a bachelor s or master s degree . Because recruitment can take place before a student s final semester, potential applicants should begin researching programs well before graduation rather than waiting until their degree has been completed. The exact qualification, graduation date and technical requirements depend upon the specific analyst position and geographical region. Associate-Level Opportunities Bank of America also provides associate-level opportunities for candidates with more advanced academic backgrounds. Associate programs are generally aimed at students pursuing qualifications such as an MBA, PhD, master s degree or another relevant advanced degree , depending on the position and region. These opportunities may be appropriate for individuals who have developed specialized academic knowledge or previous professional experience and are ready to enter the organization at an advanced early-career level. Major Career Areas Available Bank of America s student opportunities span several major areas of the organization. Banking, Markets and Finance Students interested in financial services may explore opportunities involving customers, businesses and institutional clients. Potential areas can include: Retail banking Investment banking Global markets Wealth management Corporate banking Other customer- and client-focused financial services These opportunities can be particularly relevant for students studying finance, economics, accounting, business, mathematics or related subjects, although individual job descriptions should always be reviewed for specific academic requirements. Corporate Functions Bank of America s corporate functions support the strategic and operational management of the organization. Opportunities can include areas such as auditing, digital solutions and other corporate services. Students interested in governance, administration, finance, risk, audit, strategy or business support functions may find relevant opportunities within this area. Technology and Operations Technology plays a major role in modern financial institutions, and Bank of America also recruits students for technology and operational positions. These teams support the infrastructure, technology platforms, information-security capabilities and operational systems needed to provide financial services to customers and clients. Technology-related opportunities may therefore appeal to students studying computer science, information technology, cybersecurity, engineering, data-related disciplines and similar fields. General Eligibility Requirements Although every Bank of America campus program can establish its own requirements, there is one important general eligibility condition. Applicants must normally be currently enrolled in a college, university or advanced-degree program to be considered for campus opportunities. Individuals who are no longer students can instead explore Bank of America s professional or experienced-hire opportunities. Additional eligibility requirements can depend on factors such as: Degree level Expected graduation date Academic performance Relevant technical skills Language ability Program location Business division Work authorization Professional experience Specific requirements contained in the individual job description Applicants should therefore never assume that satisfying the general student requirement automatically makes them eligible for every Bank of America program. The specific vacancy description remains the controlling source for the requirements of an individual opportunity. What Kind of Candidates Is Bank of America Looking For? Bank of America indicates that there is not one rigid candidate profile applicable to every opportunity. The bank says it values differences in areas such as thought, culture, experience and working style. Candidates should demonstrate genuine interest in the business and an ability to work effectively with others. Depending on the region and program, qualities that may be relevant include strong academic ability, professional and extracurricular achievement, integrity, teamwork, leadership, intellectual curiosity, communication abilities and interest in the relevant area of banking or business. Certain positions may also require specific technical or language capabilities. EMEA Academic Requirements Students interested in opportunities in Europe, the Middle East and Africa (EMEA) should pay particular attention to the regional requirements. For analyst opportunities, Bank of America states that candidates generally need to have obtained, or realistically expect to obtain, at least a 2:1 degree or equivalent . For MBA-level opportunities, completion of an MBA or equivalent advanced degree is required. Applicants for certain pre-internship opportunities should generally have achieved, or be on track to achieve, ABB or higher at A-level or an equivalent qualification. Bank of America notes that applicants whose results were affected by extenuating circumstances can provide relevant information in their application. Bank of America Application Process The precise recruitment process varies according to region, program and business division, but applicants can generally expect several stages. First, candidates should research the available opportunities and select the program that best matches their education, interests, location and expected graduation date. They then submit their application through Bank of America s recruitment platform. Depending on the program, the application can include a CV or résumé, competency-related questions and a digital or on-demand video interview. Candidates who successfully complete the initial screening process may progress to further interviews or assessments. These can take place by telephone, video, on campus or at a Bank of America office. Final-stage assessments can involve interviews with representatives from the business division to which the applicant has applied. Some programs or regions can also include exercises or additional assessments designed to evaluate relevant competencies and aptitude. Important Application Advice Bank of America uses rolling recruitment for a number of its programs. This means applicants should not necessarily wait until the published final deadline. Assessments can begin while applications are still open, so applying earlier can be important where applications are reviewed on a rolling basis. Applicants should carefully review the individual opportunity before submitting an application and confirm that they meet the academic, graduation-date, technical, language and location-specific requirements. Candidates should also ensure that all required components of the application are completed before the relevant deadline. Application Deadline for Bank of America Campus Programs There is no single global deadline for the Bank of America Campus Experience because the page covers multiple programs, countries and regions. Deadlines vary according to the opportunity. For the United States and Canada , application periods vary by line of business throughout the year and applications can be reviewed on a rolling basis. Bank of America advises candidates to check the individual program page for the applicable deadline. For Latin America , internship recruitment takes place on a rolling basis, with specific deadlines varying by program. For Europe, the Middle East and Africa , applications for the 2026 recruitment cycle for Summer, Off-Cycle and Full-Time programs opened on September 1, 2026 and are scheduled to close on: October 11, 2026 Bank of America states that recruitment is conducted on a rolling basis and encourages candidates to submit applications early. For Asia-Pacific , recruitment schedules vary by program and country. For Asia-Pacific markets excluding Australia, India and Japan, the currently published general recruitment windows include: Banking Connections: February to March Industrial Attachment: July to October Summer Internship: July to October Full-Time Program: July to October For Australia, the published recruitment windows are generally February to August for Summer Internships and February to April for Full-Time Programs. Candidates seeking opportunities in India are advised to consult their university careers service, while candidates interested in Japan should consult Bank of America s dedicated Japan recruitment information. Because individual vacancies can have different closing dates, applicants should always verify the deadline shown on the specific position before applying. Work Authorization and International Applicants International students should carefully examine work-authorization requirements for the country where they want to work. Policies vary considerably by location. For Asia-Pacific opportunities, Bank of America states that candidates may be considered for summer internships and full-time positions even if they do not currently have work authorization for the relevant country. However, visa-sponsorship practices remain subject to business requirements and applicable local laws. According to Bank of America s current APAC guidance, the bank can currently assist with work sponsorship for opportunities in Hong Kong, Singapore and Japan , while it does not currently support work sponsorship for opportunities in Australia . Applicants should not assume that the same sponsorship policy applies to another region or country. They should review the specific vacancy and local recruitment information before applying. Can Previous Applicants Apply Again? Yes. Bank of America states that candidates who previously applied may potentially apply again, subject to regional application limits. For example, the main campus page states that applicants may generally apply to one office and one division per year, and candidates who are unsuccessful for a summer program may apply for a Full-Time program the following year. Different regional rules can apply. For example, Bank of America s APAC guidance currently permits candidates to submit two applications per year. Applicants should therefore check the applicable rules for their region before submitting multiple applications. Benefits for Interns, Analysts and Associates Benefits vary according to employment type and location. Bank of America states that student internships do not qualify for its complete employee benefits package. However, eligible full-time analyst and associate positions may qualify for employment benefits such as health insurance, retirement-related benefits and other benefits applicable to the employee s position and location. The specific compensation and benefits associated with an individual opportunity should be confirmed from the relevant vacancy or offer documentation. Equal Employment Opportunity Bank of America states that qualified candidates are considered for employment without regard to characteristics including race, religion, color, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, national origin, ancestry, citizenship, protected veteran status or disability status, subject to applicable law. This means the Campus Experience is not presented as an opportunity limited to applicants of a particular racial or ethnic group. Eligibility instead depends primarily on the requirements of the relevant position, academic status and applicable employment or immigration requirements. How to Apply Applicants should visit the official Bank of America Campus Experience website and explore the available student opportunities. Official website: https://careers.bankofamerica.com/en-us/students/campus-experience Before applying: Identify the region where you want to work. Select your preferred career area. Determine whether you are applying for an internship, analyst, associate, placement or another student program. Review the degree and graduation-date requirements. Check technical or language requirements. Review work-authorization or visa requirements where relevant. Confirm the exact application deadline for the individual vacancy. Prepare an updated CV or résumé. Complete all required online application stages. Apply as early as possible where recruitment operates on a rolling basis. Final Thoughts The Bank of America Campus Experience provides university students and advanced-degree candidates with access to a broad portfolio of early-career opportunities across banking, financial markets, corporate functions, technology and operations. The programs are particularly relevant for students who want to combine their academic education with practical experience inside a major international financial institution. Depending on the opportunity, participants can receive professional training, mentorship, networking opportunities, hands-on experience and exposure to Bank of America s working environment. Students should remember that the Campus Experience is not one standardized global program. Eligibility requirements, recruitment periods, work-authorization conditions and application deadlines differ significantly by country, business division and program. Prospective applicants should therefore identify the specific opportunity that matches their degree level, graduation date, geographical preference and career interests, then carefully review the official vacancy before applying. For candidates interested in EMEA opportunities, the currently published closing date for the main Summer, Off-Cycle and Full-Time 2026 recruitment cycle is October 11, 2026 , and Bank of America recommends applying early because recruitment takes place on a rolling basis. title: Harvard Environmental Fellows Program 2027: $92,000 Annual Salary for Recent Doctorate Recipients
summary: The Harvard Environmental Fellows Program 2027 is now accepting applications from recent doctorate recipients and scholars with comparable terminal degrees who want to pursue independent environmental research while working with faculty across Harvard University. The two-year fellowship is designed to help early-career scholars use Harvard’s extensive academic and research resources to address complex environmental challenges through research that can connect different disciplines and professional schools. The program is offered through the Harvard University Center for the Environment (HUCE) , a center of the Salata Institute, and is expected to award approximately five fellowships for the 2027 cohort . With a salary of $92,000 per year , health insurance eligibility, relocation reimbursement, and an annual professional-expenses allowance, the fellowship provides both financial support and access to Harvard’s interdisciplinary research environment. Harvard Environmental Fellows Program 2027 Overview The Environmental Fellows Program enables recent doctoral graduates to develop their research at Harvard while working closely with a Harvard faculty host. Opportunity Details Program Harvard Environmental Fellows Program Institution Harvard University Center for the Environment Cohort 2027 Duration 2 years Salary $92,000 per year Health Insurance Employee health insurance eligibility Relocation Support Up to $2,500 Annual Professional Allowance $2,500 for travel and other professional expenses Expected Awards Approximately 5 fellowships Eligible Degree Date May 2023 – August 2027 Application Deadline December 1, 2026 Research Location Harvard University Host Required Yes What Is the Harvard Environmental Fellows Program? The Environmental Fellows Program was created by HUCE to give recent doctorate recipients the opportunity to make use of Harvard’s academic, research, and professional resources while developing work addressing complex environmental issues. Fellows spend two years working with Harvard faculty members . Importantly, the program is not restricted to one particular Harvard school or department. A fellow can potentially work with a faculty member from a wide range of academic fields. The program is intended to create connections among researchers working in different disciplines and professional schools. As a result, applicants are encouraged to develop research that can contribute to environmental scholarship or practice while also establishing connections beyond their previous academic work. Financial Benefits of the Fellowship Selected Environmental Fellows receive substantial financial and professional support throughout the fellowship. $92,000 Annual Salary Each fellow receives a salary of: $92,000 per year Because the fellowship lasts two years, the salary component represents approximately $184,000 over the full two-year period , before applicable taxes and deductions. Health Insurance Eligibility Fellows are eligible for employee health insurance , providing access to Harvard s employee benefits structure. Relocation Reimbursement The program provides reimbursement of up to: $2,500 for relocation expenses This can help eligible fellows with costs associated with relocating for the fellowship. Professional Expenses Allowance Fellows also receive: $2,500 annually for travel and other professional expenses. This support can contribute toward activities connected with professional development and research. Who Can Apply for the Harvard Environmental Fellows Program? The fellowship is open to individuals who have completed a doctorate or comparable terminal degree within the specified period. For the 2027 cohort, the degree must have been awarded between: May 2023 and August 2027 The program therefore targets scholars who are relatively early in their postdoctoral or professional careers. Eligible terminal degrees can come from a broad range of academic fields. The program specifically notes that fellows and hosts may come from areas including: Sciences Economics Law Government Public policy Public health Medicine Design Humanities Other relevant disciplines The diversity of fields reflects the program s emphasis on environmental research that can extend across traditional academic boundaries. Interdisciplinary Research Is Encouraged Applicants do not have to conduct interdisciplinary research to be considered. However, the program explicitly encourages interdisciplinary projects. This means applicants working within a single discipline can apply, while researchers who can demonstrate meaningful connections between different areas of scholarship are also encouraged to apply. For example, an environmental research proposal could potentially connect environmental science with: Public policy Economics Law Public health Government Design History or other humanities disciplines The key consideration is whether the proposed research represents a strong and independent contribution to addressing environmental issues. Research Proposal Requirements The proposed project is an important part of the selection process. HUCE faculty evaluate proposals based on several factors, including whether the project: Represents an independent line of inquiry Extends beyond the applicant s doctoral research Extends beyond the host faculty member s existing research Addresses relevant environmental issues Demonstrates strong potential for intellectual achievement Can contribute to scholarship or practice Applicants should therefore avoid simply proposing to continue their PhD research in a slightly different form. The program specifically looks for research that moves the candidate in a new direction while establishing a meaningful connection with the proposed Harvard host. Your Project Should Be Distinct From Your PhD Work One of the important features of this fellowship is the expectation that the proposed research should go beyond the applicant s previous doctoral work. The project should represent a new intellectual direction rather than simply being an extension of the PhD dissertation. This requirement is particularly important for applicants who completed their doctorate recently because the fellowship is intended to help scholars develop new research trajectories. Harvard candidates are subject to an additional expectation: their proposed research and host arrangements must take them in directions that are significantly distinct from their PhD research. Harvard Candidates The program allows candidates who received their terminal degrees from Harvard, as well as postdoctoral researchers currently working at Harvard, to apply. However, these applicants must demonstrate that the proposed fellowship would take their research in a significantly new direction. Harvard candidates should: Propose research substantially different from their PhD work Establish new research connections within the University Avoid continuing with the same professors or groups with whom they are currently associated Avoid simply extending their current research This is designed to ensure that the fellowship provides a genuinely new research opportunity. Finding a Harvard Faculty Host One of the most important steps in preparing an application is identifying a suitable Harvard faculty host . Applicants are strongly encouraged to begin this process early. The faculty host will: Mentor the fellow Provide office space Provide basic administrative support Offer a productive research environment Support the proposed research project The host s commitment is an important component of the application. Host Support Letter Every applicant s proposed host must submit a letter of support of no more than two pages . The letter should describe: The faculty member s commitment to the applicant Their commitment to the proposed research Their ability to mentor the fellow Their support for the candidate s proposed project The program notes that Harvard faculty members can receive approaches from many potential applicants and may conduct their own selection process before agreeing to recommend a candidate. How to Find a Suitable Host Applicants who are unfamiliar with Harvard faculty can explore potential hosts through the Salata Institute s faculty resources. Salata Institute Faculty Directory When identifying a potential host, applicants should carefully examine the faculty member s research interests, publications, and academic background. A strong potential host should be someone whose expertise aligns meaningfully with the proposed research while still allowing the applicant to establish an independent research direction. Importantly, faculty members from any discipline may potentially serve as hosts , regardless of whether they have previously worked specifically in environmental research or with HUCE. However, each faculty member can host only one Environmental Fellow at a time . Faculty Members Not Available as Hosts in 2027 According to the program information provided, the following faculty members are not eligible to host Environmental Fellows in 2027: Charles Davis Charles Taylor Scott Edwards Le Xie Robin Kelsey Phillip Deloria The program also states that the following faculty members have indicated that they cannot serve as hosts: Richard Lazarus — Harvard Law School Joyce Chaplin — History Applicants should therefore consider host availability before investing significant effort in approaching a particular faculty member. Selection Criteria The Environmental Fellows selection process considers the applicant s previous academic and professional achievements as well as the potential contribution of the proposed research. Key considerations include: 1. Academic and Professional Success The committee considers the applicant s previous academic and professional accomplishments. Applicants should be able to demonstrate a strong record that supports their potential as an independent scholar or practitioner. 2. Potential Contribution The committee evaluates the candidate s potential contribution to: Scholarship Environmental research Professional practice Broader understanding of environmental issues 3. Strength of the Research Proposal The proposed project should demonstrate: Independence Intellectual ambition Environmental relevance A clear departure from previous doctoral research Potential for meaningful scholarly achievement 4. Host Faculty Commitment The host s enthusiasm and commitment are also important. The committee considers whether the proposed host can: Mentor the fellow effectively Support the research Provide appropriate workspace Offer a productive research environment 5. Diversity of Research Interests HUCE aims to create a cohort with a diverse range of: Academic interests Skills Backgrounds Research approaches The 2027 cohort is expected to complement fellows selected previously, with the overall cohort consisting of approximately a dozen scholars. More information click HERE Interview Stage After reviewing applications, the selection committee will invite a selected group of applicants to discuss their proposals further. The interview will take place by video with the selection committee. Applicants should therefore be prepared to clearly explain: Their proposed research Why the project matters How it addresses an environmental issue How it differs from their PhD research Why Harvard is an appropriate environment Why the proposed faculty host is suitable What contribution they expect the project to make Fellowship Community and Harvard Faculty Engagement The Environmental Fellows Program is not limited to individual research. HUCE organizes a co-curricular program designed to help fellows become familiar with one another and with each other s research. Fellows participate in biweekly dinners involving: Environmental Fellows Harvard faculty A speaker from the Harvard faculty These activities are intended to strengthen intellectual exchange and help fellows build connections across Harvard. Other Harvard Environmental Research Opportunities The program also points prospective applicants toward the Global Change Postdoctoral Fellowship at Harvard University s Arnold Arboretum. Global Change Fellows are eligible to participate in the Environmental Fellows cohort at HUCE under the arrangements described by the program. Applicants interested in this related opportunity can explore the Arnold Arboretum s program information. Harvard Arnold Arboretum Global Change Postdoctoral Fellowship Important Deadline The application window for the 2027 Harvard Environmental Fellows Program is currently open . Application Deadline: December 1, 2026 Applicants should not wait until the final deadline to begin looking for a Harvard faculty host. Because the host relationship and faculty support letter are important parts of the application, prospective applicants should allow sufficient time to: Identify potential faculty hosts. Review their research interests. Contact suitable faculty members. Discuss the proposed research. Establish a host relationship. Develop the research proposal. Secure the required host support. Complete the application before the deadline. There is also an important program-specific note concerning the Department of the History of Science : it has a November 1 deadline for sponsor requests . Applicants considering a History of Science sponsor should therefore take this earlier date into account. How to Prepare a Strong Application Although the final selection is made by the HUCE faculty committee, applicants can use the program s stated criteria to guide their preparation. Start With the Research Question Clearly define the environmental problem or research question you want to investigate. Your project should demonstrate why the issue deserves scholarly attention and what new contribution your research could make. Make the Project Independent Avoid presenting a proposal that simply continues your doctoral dissertation. Instead, demonstrate how the fellowship would allow you to develop a new line of inquiry. Identify the Right Harvard Host Research potential faculty hosts carefully. Look beyond someone s job title and examine their: Publications Current research Academic interests Methodological expertise Connections to your proposed project Demonstrate the Harvard Connection Explain why Harvard s research environment and the proposed faculty host are particularly useful for your project. The application should make clear why this research direction benefits from the resources and intellectual environment available at Harvard. Think Across Disciplines Interdisciplinary research is encouraged, so applicants may want to identify meaningful connections between their environmental research and other fields. However, interdisciplinary work is not mandatory . A strong single-discipline proposal can also be considered. Who Is This Fellowship For? The Harvard Environmental Fellows Program is particularly relevant to recent doctorate recipients or scholars with comparable terminal degrees who want to establish an independent research direction focused on environmental issues. The program can be relevant to researchers working across a remarkably broad range of fields, including science, economics, law, government, public policy, public health, medicine, design, and the humanities. The fellowship may therefore be particularly useful for scholars whose environmental research does not fit neatly into one academic discipline. Application Information The official application is available through Harvard University s academic positions system. Harvard Environmental Fellows Program Application For questions about the program, applicants can contact: Jim Clem HUCE Managing Director environmental_fellows@harvard.edu The main program page is available through the Harvard University Center for the Environment. Harvard University Center for the Environment – Environmental Fellows Program Conclusion The Harvard Environmental Fellows Program 2027 provides recent doctorate recipients with a two-year opportunity to develop independent environmental research within Harvard s interdisciplinary academic environment. Fellows receive a $92,000 annual salary , health insurance eligibility, relocation support of up to $2,500, and a $2,500 annual allowance for travel and professional expenses. A particularly important feature of the program is its emphasis on independent research that moves beyond the applicant s PhD work . Applicants should therefore begin preparing early, especially when identifying a Harvard faculty host and developing a proposal that demonstrates both environmental relevance and intellectual independence. With approximately five fellowships expected for the 2027 cohort, prospective applicants should carefully review the eligibility requirements, establish a suitable host relationship, and prepare their materials well before the December 1, 2026 deadline .
